events.name: 2023 Marrakesh–Safi earthquake
events.enhanced_description: A powerful 6.9 magnitude earthquake struck the Marrakesh–Safi province in western Morocco, resulting in the tragic loss of at least 2,960 lives and extensive damage to historic buildings. The earthquake underscored the region's vulnerability to seismic activity.

events.name: G20 summit in New Delhi
events.enhanced_description: At the 18th G20 summit held in New Delhi, the African Union was announced as the 21st permanent member of the G20. This decision reflects a significant step towards greater representation of African nations in global economic discussions.

events.name: 2023 Swiss federal election
events.enhanced_description: In the 2023 Swiss federal election, the Swiss People's Party successfully retained its majority in the National Council, solidifying its position as the leading political force in Switzerland. This election reflects the ongoing political dynamics and voter sentiments in the country.

events.name: Hurricane Otis landfall
events.enhanced_description: Hurricane Otis made landfall near Acapulco, Mexico, becoming the most powerful Eastern Pacific hurricane to do so, with winds reaching 165 mph. The storm resulted in significant devastation and at least 80 fatalities, highlighting the increasing intensity of tropical cyclones in the region.

events.name: Israel intercepts Houthi missile
events.enhanced_description: In a significant military event, Israel successfully intercepted a ballistic missile launched by the Yemeni Houthi movement using its Arrow 2 missile defense system. This interception, occurring above the Negev Desert, marked a historic first instance of combat occurring in space.

events.name: First AI Safety Summit
events.enhanced_description: The first AI Safety Summit convened in London, where representatives from 28 countries signed a landmark agreement aimed at managing the risks associated with advanced artificial intelligence technologies. This summit underscored the global commitment to ensuring safe AI development.

events.name: The Beatles release 'Now and Then'
events.enhanced_description: The Beatles released 'Now and Then', their final song, featuring restored vocals by John Lennon and guitar tracks by George Harrison. This release marked a poignant moment in music history, celebrating the band's enduring legacy.

events.name: Israel–Hamas war death toll

locations.name: Gaza City, Gaza Strip, State of Palestine

events.enhanced_description: The ongoing Israel–Hamas conflict saw the death toll in Gaza surpass 10,000, prompting United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres to call for a humanitarian ceasefire to facilitate aid delivery to affected civilians. This tragic milestone highlights the severe humanitarian crisis in the region.

events.name: António Costa announces resignation
events.enhanced_description: Portuguese Prime Minister António Costa announced his impending resignation, leading to the President of Portugal dissolving parliament and calling for early elections scheduled for March 10, 2024. This political shift signals a significant change in the Portuguese government landscape.

events.name: World's first whole eye transplant

locations.name: Metropolitan Museum of Art
locations.historical_name: Bacchanal: A Faun Teased by Children

events.enhanced_description: Surgeons at NYU Langone Health in New York City announced the successful completion of the world's first whole eye transplant, marking a groundbreaking achievement in medical science and organ transplantation. This procedure opens new avenues for treating severe eye conditions.

events.name: Falepili Union treaty
events.enhanced_description: In a historic agreement known as the Falepili Union treaty, Australia granted special rights to Tuvaluans, allowing them freedom of movement and defense rights for residence and employment due to climate change impacts. This treaty reflects the growing recognition of climate refugees.

events.name: APEC summit in San Francisco
events.enhanced_description: President Joe Biden hosted the APEC summit in San Francisco, attended by Chinese President Xi Jinping. The summit concluded with agreements to reopen military communication channels and collaborate on climate change, indicating a thaw in U.S.-China relations.

events.name: Global temperature exceeds 2°C
events.enhanced_description: For the first time in recorded history, the global average temperature temporarily exceeded 2°C above the pre-industrial average, underscoring the urgent climate crisis facing the planet. This milestone raises alarms about the impacts of climate change on ecosystems and human societies.

events.name: 2023 Argentine presidential election
events.enhanced_description: In the 2023 Argentine presidential election, Javier Milei emerged victorious in the second round, set to assume office on December 10, 2023, alongside his vice president, Victoria Villarruel. This election reflects a significant shift in Argentina's political landscape.

events.name: Boeing P-8A Poseidon incident

locations.name: Marine Corps Air Station Kaneohe Bay, Kaneohe, Hawaii, United States

events.enhanced_description: A Boeing P-8A Poseidon aircraft operated by the United States Navy overshot the runway at Marine Corps Air Station Kaneohe Bay in Hawaii. Fortunately, there were no fatalities reported in this incident, highlighting the importance of safety protocols in military aviation.

events.name: Israel and Hamas ceasefire agreement

locations.name: Gaza City, Gaza Strip, State of Palestine

events.enhanced_description: Israel and Hamas reached a significant four-day ceasefire agreement, marking the first pause in hostilities since October 7. During this period, many Israeli hostages were set to be released in exchange for Palestinian prisoners, offering a glimmer of hope amidst ongoing conflict.

events.name: Riots in Dublin after mass stabbing
events.enhanced_description: Riots erupted in Dublin following a mass stabbing incident on Parnell Square East, which resulted in injuries to four individuals. The unrest reflects underlying tensions within the community and raises concerns about public safety.

events.name: Somalia joins East African Community
events.enhanced_description: Somalia was officially admitted as the eighth member of the East African Community, a significant step in regional integration following its application for membership in 2012. This membership aims to enhance cooperation and development among East African nations.

events.name: Christopher Luxon sworn in as Prime Minister of New Zealand
events.enhanced_description: Christopher Luxon was sworn in as the 42nd Prime Minister of New Zealand after forming a coalition government with the right-wing ACT and New Zealand First parties. His administration faces criticism for its stance on Māori culture and social equity issues.

events.name: Brazil joins OPEC+
events.enhanced_description: Brazil announced its intention to join OPEC+ during a meeting in Vienna, where the organization discussed oil output strategies for 2024. As the largest oil producer in South America, Brazil's membership is expected to influence global oil markets.

events.name: 2023 Guyana–Venezuela crisis referendum
events.enhanced_description: In a symbolic referendum, Venezuelans voted on the creation of a subdivision in the disputed territory of Guayana Esequiba, currently controlled by Guyana. Analysts suggest that the referendum's practical implications are likely to be minimal, reflecting ongoing tensions between the two nations.

events.name: Google DeepMind releases Gemini Language Model
events.enhanced_description: Google DeepMind unveiled the Gemini Language Model, designed to serve as a foundational model integrated into Google's suite of tools, including Search and Bard. This release represents a significant advancement in artificial intelligence capabilities.

events.name: 2023 Egyptian presidential election
events.enhanced_description: In the 2023 Egyptian presidential election, incumbent President Abdel Fattah el-Sisi secured a third term with 89.6% of the vote, reinforcing his grip on power amid ongoing political challenges in the country. This election reflects the current political climate in Egypt.

events.name: COP28 climate summit agreement
events.enhanced_description: At the COP28 climate summit held in Dubai, a historic consensus was reached among countries to transition away from fossil fuels, marking the first such agreement in the conference's 30-year history. This agreement focuses on energy systems, excluding sectors like plastics and agriculture.

events.name: Death of Emir of Kuwait

locations.name: Kuwait City, Al Asimah Governorate, Kuwait

coordinate_source.cache_key: Kuwait City, Al Asimah Governorate, Kuwait

events.enhanced_description: Emir of Kuwait, Nawaf Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah, passed away at the age of 86, leading to the succession of his half-brother, Mishal Al-Ahmad Al-Jaber Al-Sabah. This transition marks a significant moment in Kuwaiti politics and governance.

events.name: 2023 Serbian parliamentary election
events.enhanced_description: The 2023 Serbian parliamentary election was held on December 17, 2023, resulting in the SNS coalition, led by Miloš Vučević, securing 128 out of 250 seats in the Serbian National Assembly. This election was significant in shaping the political landscape of Serbia amidst ongoing domestic and international challenges.

events.name: Suspension of shipping operations in the Red Sea
events.enhanced_description: On December 18, 2023, several shipping companies announced a temporary suspension of their operations in the Red Sea due to ongoing attacks on vessels by Houthi rebels. This decision highlighted the escalating security concerns in the region and its impact on international shipping routes.

events.name: 2023 Democratic Republic of the Congo general election

locations.name: Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo

coordinate_source.cache_key: Kinshasa, Democratic Republic of the Congo

events.enhanced_description: The 2023 general election in the Democratic Republic of the Congo took place on December 20, 2023, where incumbent President Félix Tshisekedi was re-elected, defeating two major challengers. This election was crucial for the stability of the country amidst ongoing political tensions.

events.name: European Court of Justice ruling on European Super League
events.enhanced_description: On December 21, 2023, the European Court of Justice ruled that threats by FIFA and UEFA to sanction football clubs wishing to join the European Super League were unlawful. This landmark decision had significant implications for the governance of football in Europe.

events.name: Prague university mass shooting
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2023, the deadliest mass shooting in the Czech Republic's history occurred at a university in Prague, resulting in 15 fatalities and 25 injuries. This tragic event raised concerns about gun violence and security in educational institutions.

events.name: Russian invasion of Ukraine drone and missile assault
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2023, Russia launched a significant wave of drone and missile strikes on Ukrainian cities, resulting in numerous casualties. This marked a critical moment in the ongoing conflict, with Ukraine responding with its own drone assaults the following day.

events.name: Genocide case against Israel at the International Court of Justice
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2023, South Africa brought a genocide case against Israel to the International Court of Justice, citing the humanitarian crisis resulting from Israel's invasion and bombardment of the Gaza Strip. This case underscores the international legal challenges surrounding the conflict.

events.name: Queen Margrethe II of Denmark abdication announcement
events.enhanced_description: On December 31, 2023, Queen Margrethe II of Denmark announced her abdication, effective January 14, 2024, after 52 years on the throne. This announcement marked the end of a significant era in Danish history.

events.name: BRICS membership expansion
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates officially became members of BRICS, a significant expansion of the group aimed at enhancing cooperation among emerging economies.

events.name: 2023 Marshallese general election
events.enhanced_description: In the 2023 Marshallese general election held on January 2, 2024, the Legislature of the Marshall Islands elected Hilda Heine as President for a second non-consecutive term. This election was pivotal for the political landscape of the Marshall Islands.

events.name: 2024 Kerman bombings
events.enhanced_description: On January 3, 2024, an Islamic State double bombing in Kerman, Iran, killed 94 people during a memorial event for Qasem Soleimani. The attack involved two briefcase bombs detonated remotely, highlighting the ongoing threat of terrorism in the region.

events.name: 2024 Bangladeshi general election
events.enhanced_description: On January 7, 2024, the Awami League, led by incumbent Sheikh Hasina, won a fourth consecutive term in the Bangladeshi general election amid protests from opposition parties and a significant drop in voter turnout. This election was critical for the political stability of Bangladesh.

events.name: 2024 conflict in Ecuador
events.enhanced_description: On January 8, 2024, Ecuadorian President Daniel Noboa declared a state of emergency following the escape of drug cartel leader José Adolfo Macías Villamar from prison. The declaration involved military deployment and a national nighttime curfew to restore order.

events.name: Riots in Papua New Guinea

locations.name: Seeadler Harbor, Manus Province, Papua New Guinea

coordinate_source.cache_key: Seeadler Harbor, Manus Province, Papua New Guinea

events.enhanced_description: On January 11, 2024, riots erupted across Papua New Guinea after an alleged rounding error led to pay cuts for police officers and soldiers. The unrest highlighted the tensions between the government and its security forces.

events.name: Operation Prosperity Guardian
events.enhanced_description: On January 12, 2024, a U.S.-led coalition launched airstrikes against Houthi militant locations in Yemen, marking a retaliation for the Houthis' attacks on ships in the Red Sea. This operation underscored the ongoing conflict in the region.

events.name: 2024 Taiwanese presidential election
events.enhanced_description: On January 13, 2024, Lai Ching-te of the ruling Democratic Progressive Party won the Taiwanese presidential election with 40% of the vote. This election was significant in determining Taiwan's political direction amidst rising tensions with China.

events.name: Margrethe II abdication as Queen of Denmark
events.enhanced_description: On January 14, 2024, Margrethe II formally abdicated as Queen of Denmark, marking the end of her 52-year reign. Her eldest son, Frederik, succeeded her as King Frederik X, ushering in a new era for the Danish monarchy.

events.name: Inauguration of Bernardo Arévalo as President of Guatemala

locations.name: Universidad de San Carlos de Guatemala, Guatemala City

coordinate_source.cache_key: Universidad de San Carlos de Guatemala, Guatemala City

events.enhanced_description: On January 15, 2024, Bernardo Arévalo was inaugurated as the 52nd President of Guatemala following a brief political crisis after the 2023 elections. His presidency is seen as a pivotal moment for the country's democratic processes.

events.name: Iran missile and drone strikes in Pakistan
events.enhanced_description: On January 16, 2024, Iran conducted a series of missile and drone strikes in Pakistan's Balochistan province, claiming to target the Iranian Baloch militant group Jaish ul-Adl. This operation escalated tensions between the two neighboring countries.

events.name: Pakistan retaliatory airstrikes on Iran
events.enhanced_description: On January 18, 2024, Pakistan conducted retaliatory airstrikes on Iran's Sistan and Baluchestan province following Iran's missile and drone strikes. This exchange marked a significant escalation in the ongoing tensions between the two nations.

events.name: Japan's SLIM mission soft landing on the Moon
events.enhanced_description: On January 19, 2024, Japan achieved a historic milestone by becoming the fifth country to successfully execute a soft landing on the Moon with its SLIM mission. This accomplishment marked a significant advancement in space exploration technology.

events.name: 2024 Korochansky Ilyushin Il-76 crash
events.enhanced_description: On January 24, 2024, a Russian Ilyushin Il-76 military transport plane crashed in the Korochansky District, reportedly carrying 65 Ukrainian prisoners of war along with crew members and guards, resulting in the death of all on board. This incident raised serious concerns regarding the treatment of prisoners in the ongoing conflict.

events.name: Israel–Hamas war: The UN's International Court of Justice ruling
events.enhanced_description: On January 26, 2024, the International Court of Justice ruled that Israel must take all necessary measures to prevent genocidal acts in Gaza, amidst ongoing conflict with Hamas. However, the court did not mandate an immediate cessation of military operations, reflecting the complex legal and political dynamics of the situation.

events.name: Sultan of Johor Ibrahim Iskandar ascends the throne
events.enhanced_description: On January 31, 2024, Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar of Johor was formally proclaimed as the 17th Yang di-Pertuan Agong of Malaysia, succeeding the previous king. His ascension marks a significant moment in Malaysian constitutional monarchy, where the king is elected from among the nine Malay state rulers.

events.name: Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran and the United Arab Emirates become BRICS members
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, Egypt, Ethiopia, Iran, and the United Arab Emirates officially joined the BRICS group, expanding the coalition of major emerging economies. This expansion reflects the growing influence of these nations in global economic discussions and their desire for greater representation on the world stage.

events.name: Dissolution of the Republic of Artsakh
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, the Republic of Artsakh was formally dissolved following Azerbaijan's military recapture of the region. This event marked a significant shift in the geopolitical landscape of the South Caucasus, ending a long-standing territorial dispute.

events.name: 7.5 Mww earthquake strikes Japan
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, a powerful 7.5 magnitude earthquake struck the western coast of Japan, particularly affecting the Noto Peninsula. The disaster resulted in at least 504 fatalities and thousands of injuries, highlighting the region's vulnerability to seismic activity.

events.name: Ethiopia-Somaliland port agreement
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, Ethiopia announced a significant agreement with Somaliland to utilize the port of Berbera, marking a pivotal moment in regional trade dynamics. This agreement also included Ethiopia's intention to recognize Somaliland's independence, a first for any country.

events.name: Margrethe II abdicates as Queen of Denmark
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, Margrethe II formally abdicated the throne of Denmark after 52 years of reign, passing the crown to her eldest son, Frederik, who became King Frederik X. This transition marks a historic moment in Danish monarchy, reflecting a generational change.

events.name: Azali Assoumani wins re-election in Comoros
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, incumbent president Azali Assoumani was re-elected amid an opposition boycott, securing 62.9% of the vote with a notably low voter turnout of 16.3%. This election highlighted ongoing political tensions in the Comoros.

events.name: Israel–Hamas war: UN's International Court of Justice ruling
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, the International Court of Justice ruled that Israel must take all necessary measures to prevent genocidal acts in Gaza, amidst ongoing conflict with Hamas. However, the court did not mandate an immediate cessation of military operations, reflecting the complex legal and political dynamics of the situation.

events.name: Kausea Natano loses reelection in Tuvalu
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, Kausea Natano, the incumbent Prime Minister of Tuvalu, lost his reelection bid to Parliament. This political shift set the stage for Feleti Teo's election as the new prime minister a month later.

events.name: US airstrikes in Iraq and Syria
events.enhanced_description: On February 2, 2024, the United States launched airstrikes on 85 targets in Iraq and Syria in retaliation for a deadly drone attack on a US military base. This military action underscores the ongoing tensions and conflicts in the region.

events.name: Hage Geingob dies as President of Namibia
events.enhanced_description: On February 4, 2024, Hage Geingob, the President of Namibia, passed away at the age of 82. His vice-president, Nangolo Mbumba, succeeded him, marking a significant transition in Namibian leadership.

events.name: Sebastián Piñera dies in helicopter crash
events.enhanced_description: On February 6, 2024, former Chilean President Sebastián Piñera tragically died in a helicopter crash at the age of 74. His death shocked the nation and drew attention to his controversial political legacy.

events.name: Ilham Aliyev re-elected in Azerbaijan
events.enhanced_description: On February 7, 2024, President Ilham Aliyev was re-elected for a fifth term amid an opposition boycott, reflecting the ongoing political challenges in Azerbaijan. His administration has faced criticism for its handling of dissent and democratic processes.

events.name: Alexander Stubb elected in Finnish presidential election
events.enhanced_description: On February 11, 2024, Alexander Stubb was elected president in the closest presidential election in Finnish history, highlighting the competitive political landscape in Finland. His victory represents a significant moment for the nation's governance.

events.name: Prabowo Subianto wins Indonesian presidential election
events.enhanced_description: On February 14, 2024, Prabowo Subianto won the presidential election in Indonesia, marking a significant political shift in the country. His victory, alongside the Democratic Party of Struggle's success in the legislative election, indicates a changing political landscape.

events.name: Alexei Navalny dies under mysterious circumstances
events.enhanced_description: On February 16, 2024, Russian opposition leader Alexei Navalny died under mysterious circumstances at the age of 47. His death raised international concerns regarding political repression in Russia and the safety of dissenting voices.

events.name: Intuitive Machines' Nova-C lander lands on the Moon
events.enhanced_description: On February 22, 2024, Intuitive Machines' Nova-C lander made history by becoming the first commercial vehicle to successfully land on the Moon. This achievement marks a significant milestone in the commercialization of space exploration.

events.name: 2024 Haitian jailbreak and state of emergency
events.enhanced_description: On February 28, 2024, a state of emergency was declared in Haiti after gangs stormed two prisons, demanding the resignation of Prime Minister Ariel Henry. This incident highlights the ongoing security crisis and challenges faced by the Haitian government.

events.name: Israel–Hamas war: IDF opens fire in Gaza City
events.enhanced_description: On February 29, 2024, soldiers of the Israel Defense Forces opened fire on a crowd of civilians in Gaza City, resulting in over 100 deaths as the Palestinian casualties of the ongoing conflict exceeded 30,000. This tragic event underscores the humanitarian crisis in the region.

events.name: Nayib Bukele re-elected in El Salvador
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, incumbent President Nayib Bukele won re-election with over 80% of the vote, becoming the first president to be re-elected in El Salvador since 1944. His victory reflects his popularity and the political landscape of the country.

events.name: Sweden joins NATO
events.enhanced_description: On March 7, 2024, Sweden officially joined NATO as its 32nd member, following Finland's accession a year earlier. This historic move marks a significant shift in Sweden's long-standing policy of military non-alignment.

events.name: 2024 Portuguese legislative election
events.enhanced_description: On March 10, 2024, the Democratic Alliance won a plurality of seats in the Portuguese legislative election, forming a minority government amid losses for the incumbent Socialist Party. This election reflects the shifting political dynamics in Portugal.

events.name: Ariel Henry announces resignation
events.enhanced_description: Amid a severe crisis characterized by rampant gang violence, Ariel Henry, the acting Prime Minister of Haiti, announces his intention to resign from both his roles. This decision comes as the country grapples with escalating instability and public unrest.

events.name: Artificial Intelligence Act passed
events.enhanced_description: The European Union passes the Artificial Intelligence Act, marking a significant milestone as the world's first comprehensive legal and regulatory framework for artificial intelligence. This legislation aims to ensure the safe and ethical use of AI technologies across member states.

events.name: UN estimates civilian casualties in Israel–Hamas war

events.enhanced_description: The United Nations releases an estimate indicating that at least 56% of Palestinian civilians killed during the ongoing Israel–Hamas conflict are women and children. This statistic highlights the severe humanitarian impact of the conflict.

events.name: 2024 Russian presidential election
events.enhanced_description: In the 2024 Russian presidential election, incumbent Vladimir Putin is reelected for a fifth term, continuing his long-standing dominance in Russian politics. The election results further solidify his grip on power amidst ongoing controversies regarding electoral integrity.

events.name: Crocus City Hall attack
events.enhanced_description: Islamic State-affiliated gunmen launch a brutal attack on concertgoers at Crocus City Hall in Krasnogorsk, resulting in the deaths of at least 145 individuals and injuring over 550. This incident underscores the ongoing threat of terrorism in Russia.

events.name: 2024 Senegalese presidential election
events.enhanced_description: In the 2024 Senegalese presidential election, Bassirou Diomaye Faye is elected president following the disqualification of his party and its former candidate, Ousmane Sonko. This election marks a significant shift in Senegal's political landscape.

events.name: UN Security Council resolution on Gaza

locations.name: Metropolitan Museum of Art

events.enhanced_description: The UN Security Council passes a resolution calling for an immediate ceasefire in Gaza and demanding the unconditional release of all hostages. This resolution reflects the international community's concern over the escalating violence in the region.

events.name: Francis Scott Key Bridge collapse
events.enhanced_description: A tragic incident occurs when a container ship collides with the Francis Scott Key Bridge in Baltimore, resulting in the total collapse of the bridge and the deaths of six individuals. This disaster raises concerns about maritime safety and infrastructure integrity.

events.name: Bulgaria and Romania join Schengen Area
events.enhanced_description: Bulgaria and Romania officially become members of the Schengen Area, allowing for free movement across their borders through sea and air routes. This accession marks a significant step in their integration into the European Union.

events.name: CHP local elections victory
events.enhanced_description: In a significant political shift, the Republican People's Party (CHP) wins 37.8% of the vote in local elections, marking its first victory in a popular vote since 1977. This election represents a notable defeat for the ruling Justice and Development Party (AKP).

events.name: Israel attacks Iranian embassy
events.enhanced_description: In a military escalation, Israel conducts an airstrike on the Iranian embassy in Damascus, resulting in the deaths of 16 individuals. This attack is part of the broader conflict between Israel and Iran, heightening tensions in the region.

events.name: Taiwan earthquake
events.enhanced_description: A powerful earthquake with a magnitude of 7.4 strikes off the eastern coast of Taiwan, generating small tsunamis that reach heights of 20–30 cm in Okinawa Prefecture, Japan. This natural disaster raises concerns about seismic activity in the region.

events.name: 2024 Kuwaiti general election
events.enhanced_description: In the 2024 Kuwaiti general election, opposition candidates successfully maintain a majority in the National Assembly. This election reflects the ongoing political dynamics and challenges faced by the ruling government.

events.name: Ecuador police raid Mexican embassy
events.enhanced_description: Ecuadorian police conduct a controversial raid on the Mexican embassy in Quito to arrest former vice-president Jorge Glas, who had been granted political asylum by Mexico. This action violates the Vienna Convention on Diplomatic Relations, leading to a diplomatic crisis.

events.name: Peter Pellegrini elected President of Slovakia
events.enhanced_description: Peter Pellegrini is elected President of Slovakia in the second round of the 2024 Slovak presidential election, marking a significant political transition in the country. His election reflects the changing political landscape in Slovakia.

events.name: Total solar eclipse visible across North America
events.enhanced_description: A total solar eclipse captivates millions as it becomes visible across North America, drawing attention from astronomers and the general public alike. This astronomical event highlights the beauty and wonder of celestial phenomena.

events.name: Simon Harris becomes Taoiseach
events.enhanced_description: Following the resignation of Leo Varadkar, Simon Harris of Fine Gael is appointed as Ireland's youngest Taoiseach after a Dáil vote of 88–69. His appointment signifies a new chapter in Irish politics.

events.name: 2024 South Korean legislative election
events.enhanced_description: In the 2024 South Korean legislative election, the Democratic Party and Democratic Alliance secure 176 seats, while the ruling People Power Party and its affiliate win only 108 seats. This election reflects a significant shift in the political balance of power in South Korea.

events.name: Iran retaliates against Israel
events.enhanced_description: In response to an Israeli airstrike on the Iranian consulate in Damascus, Iran launches retaliatory strikes against Israel. This escalation further intensifies the ongoing conflict between the two nations.

events.name: 2024 Persian Gulf floods
events.enhanced_description: Heavy rainfall strikes the Middle East, resulting in severe flooding that claims at least 32 lives and disrupts operations for Emirates Airlines at Dubai International Airport. This disaster highlights the region's vulnerability to extreme weather events.

events.name: 2024 Solomon Islands general election
events.enhanced_description: In the 2024 Solomon Islands general election, incumbent Prime Minister Manasseh Sogavare's OUR Party wins a plurality of seats, maintaining its position in the government. This election reflects the ongoing political dynamics in the Solomon Islands.

events.name: Israel conducts airstrikes against Iran
events.enhanced_description: In a continuation of hostilities, Israel conducts airstrikes against Iran following a missile and drone attack on its territory. This military action escalates the ongoing conflict and raises tensions in the region.

events.name: Transitional Presidential Council takes power in Haiti
events.enhanced_description: Following the resignation of Ariel Henry, Haiti's acting Prime Minister, a Transitional Presidential Council assumes power as the new head of state. This transition aims to stabilize the country amid ongoing crises.

events.name: The G7 countries agree to phase out unabated coal power by 2030–2035
events.enhanced_description: In April 2024, during the G7 summit held in Hiroshima, Japan, the leaders of the G7 countries reached a historic agreement to phase out unabated coal power by 2030 to 2035, marking a significant step towards combating climate change and promoting sustainable energy practices.

events.name: Islands general election: Incumbent Prime Minister Manasseh Sogavare's OUR Party wins a plurality of seats
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, the Islands general election resulted in a plurality of seats for the incumbent Prime Minister Manasseh Sogavare's OUR Party, solidifying his position in the Solomon Islands' political landscape.

events.name: Parliamentary election: Incumbent Prime Minister Andrej Plenković's Croatian Democratic Union coalition wins a plurality of seats
events.enhanced_description: In the parliamentary elections held on January 1, 2024, the Croatian Democratic Union coalition, led by incumbent Prime Minister Andrej Plenković, secured a plurality of seats, reinforcing its influence in Croatian politics.

events.name: Railway embankment failure near Mai Mahiu, Kenya
events.enhanced_description: In January 2024, a railway embankment failure near Mai Mahiu, Kenya, resulted in multiple casualties, with reports of 84 individuals missing, amidst widespread flooding that had already claimed 488 lives across Kenya and Tanzania.

events.name: 2024 Panamanian general election: José Raúl Mulino is elected president
events.enhanced_description: On May 5, 2024, José Raúl Mulino was elected president of Panama in a general election, marking a significant political transition in the country's leadership.

events.name: 2024 Chadian presidential election: Mahamat Déby wins election to a full term as president
events.enhanced_description: On May 6, 2024, Mahamat Déby was elected to a full term as president of Chad, succeeding his late father Idriss Déby, in a pivotal moment for the nation's leadership.

events.name: Eurovision Song Contest 2024 held in Malmö, Sweden
events.enhanced_description: The Eurovision Song Contest 2024 took place on May 7 in Malmö, Sweden, where the Swiss contestant Nemo triumphed with the song 'The Code', showcasing the vibrant cultural exchange characteristic of the event.

events.name: North Macedonian elections: VMRO-DPMNE wins parliamentary elections
events.enhanced_description: In the North Macedonian elections held on May 8, 2024, the right-wing party VMRO-DPMNE achieved a landslide victory in parliamentary elections, while Gordana Siljanovska-Davkova was elected as the first female president of the country.

events.name: UN General Assembly grants Palestine the right to be seated among member states

locations.historical_name: Bacchanal: A Faun Teased by Children

events.enhanced_description: On May 10, 2024, the United Nations General Assembly passed a resolution granting the State of Palestine the right to be seated among member states in alphabetical order, a significant step in international recognition.

events.name: Lee Hsien Loong succeeded by Lawrence Wong as Prime Minister of Singapore

events.enhanced_description: On November 16, 2024, Gabon held a constitutional referendum that was approved by voters, marking a significant step in the country's political evolution and governance structure.

events.name: 2024 Senegalese parliamentary election: President Bassirou Diomaye Faye's party wins an absolute majority
events.enhanced_description: On November 17, 2024, Senegal held its parliamentary elections, where President Bassirou Diomaye Faye's party PASTEF won an absolute majority in the National Assembly, solidifying his political power.

events.name: The International Criminal Court (ICC) issues arrest warrants against Israeli leaders
events.enhanced_description: On November 21, 2024, the International Criminal Court issued arrest warrants against Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, former Defense Minister Yoav Gallant, and Hamas military leader Mohammed Deif for alleged war crimes committed during the Israel–Hamas War.

events.name: 2024 Uruguayan general election: Leftist opposition candidate Yamandú Orsi is elected president
events.enhanced_description: On November 24, 2024, Uruguay held its general election, resulting in the election of leftist opposition candidate Yamandú Orsi as president. His victory marked a significant political shift in the country.

events.name: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announces a ceasefire deal with Hezbollah
events.enhanced_description: On November 26, 2024, Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu announced that a ceasefire deal had been reached to end the ongoing fighting with Hezbollah in Lebanon, a significant development in regional tensions.

events.name: 2024 Namibian general election: Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah is elected as the first female president of Namibia
events.enhanced_description: On November 27, 2024, Namibia held its general election, resulting in the election of Netumbo Nandi-Ndaitwah of the SWAPO party as the first female president of Namibia, marking a historic milestone for gender representation in the country's leadership.

events.name: 2024 Irish general election: Fianna Fáil remains the largest party
events.enhanced_description: On November 29, 2024, Ireland held its general election, where the centre-right party Fianna Fáil maintained its status as the largest party in Dáil Éireann, increasing its number of seats to 48 amidst a competitive political landscape.

events.name: 2024 Icelandic parliamentary election: Social Democratic Alliance wins 15 seats
events.enhanced_description: On November 30, 2024, Iceland held its parliamentary elections, where the opposition party Social Democratic Alliance won 15 seats in the Althing, while the incumbent Independence Party secured 14 seats, resulting in a fragmented parliament without a clear majority.

events.name: Dismissal of Christian Lindner
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, German Chancellor Olaf Scholz dismissed Christian Lindner, the leader of the Free Democratic Party (FDP), from his role as finance minister. This decision led to the resignation of two other FDP ministers and ultimately resulted in the collapse of the governing coalition, significantly impacting German politics.

events.name: Gabonese Constitutional Referendum
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, a constitutional referendum was held in Gabon, resulting in its approval. This referendum was a significant step in the country's political landscape, reflecting the will of the Gabonese people regarding constitutional reforms.

events.name: Boualem Sansal Custody
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, Boualem Sansal, a French-Algerian dissident writer, was taken into custody by Algerian authorities upon his arrival in Algiers. His detention raised concerns about freedom of expression and the treatment of dissent in Algeria.

events.name: ICC Arrest Warrants
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, the International Criminal Court (ICC) issued arrest warrants for Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu, former Defense Minister Yoav Gallant, and Hamas military leader Mohammed Deif. These warrants were based on accusations of war crimes committed during the ongoing Israel–Hamas conflict.

events.name: Peshawar Terrorist Ambush

locations.name: North-West Frontier Province, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan

coordinate_source.cache_key: North-West Frontier Province, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, Pakistan

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, terrorists ambushed a convoy of vehicles carrying Shiite Muslims in Peshawar, Pakistan, resulting in the deaths of 46 individuals and injuring 20 others. This attack highlighted the ongoing sectarian violence in the region.

events.name: First Close-Up Image of WOH G64
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, researchers using the Very Large Telescope in the Atacama Desert announced the first-ever close-up image of the star WOH G64, located outside the Milky Way Galaxy. This groundbreaking achievement marked a significant milestone in astronomical imaging.

events.name: Icelandic Parliamentary Election
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, the opposition party Social Democratic Alliance won 15 seats in the Althing, Iceland's parliament, while the incumbent Independence Party secured 14 seats. However, no party achieved a majority, leading to a fragmented political landscape.

events.name: Aleppo Control Seizure
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, opposition forces seized control of most of Aleppo, Syria, prompting the first Russian airstrikes on the city since 2016. This marked a significant escalation in the ongoing Syrian civil war.

events.name: Romanian Parliamentary Election
events.enhanced_description: On December 1, 2024, the incumbent National Coalition for Romania won a plurality of votes in the parliamentary election, while far-right parties made substantial gains. This election reflected shifting political dynamics in Romania.

events.name: South Korean Martial Law Declaration
events.enhanced_description: On December 3, 2024, South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol declared martial law during a live broadcast, accusing the main opposition Democratic Party of anti-state activities. This declaration led to significant political turmoil and the signing of an impeachment article by Speaker Woo Won-shik.

events.name: Romanian Presidential Election Results Annulled
events.enhanced_description: On December 6, 2024, the Constitutional Court of Romania annulled the results of the first round of the presidential election amid accusations of Russian interference. This decision raised concerns about the integrity of the electoral process.

events.name: Ghanaian General Election
events.enhanced_description: On December 7, 2024, John Mahama of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) was elected president of Ghana for a second non-consecutive term. His victory marked a significant moment in Ghanaian politics.

events.name: Bashar al-Assad Overthrown
events.enhanced_description: On December 8, 2024, President Bashar al-Assad was overthrown in Damascus, marking the end of his presidency and the Ba'athist regime after 61 years. The Syrian opposition subsequently formed the Syrian Transitional Government as a provisional authority.

events.name: 2030 World Cup Announcement
events.enhanced_description: On December 11, 2024, FIFA announced that Morocco, Portugal, and Spain would jointly host the 2030 World Cup, with anniversary matches to be held in Argentina, Paraguay, and Uruguay. Additionally, Saudi Arabia was confirmed as the host for the 2034 World Cup.

events.name: Gukesh Dommaraju Chess Championship
events.enhanced_description: On December 12, 2024, Indian chess prodigy Gukesh Dommaraju defeated former world champion Ding Liren in the World Chess Championship, becoming the youngest champion at 18 years and 195 days old, breaking Garry Kasparov's previous record.

events.name: Georgian Presidential Election
events.enhanced_description: On December 14, 2024, Mikheil Kavelashvili of the People's Power party was elected unopposed as the president of Georgia, marking a significant moment in the country's political landscape.

events.name: Port Vila Earthquake
events.enhanced_description: On December 17, 2024, the capital of Vanuatu, Port Vila, suffered extensive damage after a Mw 7.3 earthquake, resulting in at least 16 fatalities. This natural disaster highlighted the region's vulnerability to seismic activity.

events.name: Political Asylum Granted
events.enhanced_description: On December 19, 2024, the Hungarian government, led by Viktor Orbán, granted political asylum to Polish MP Marcin Romanowski, who was wanted on an European Arrest Warrant for alleged fraud. This decision raised questions about Hungary's stance on European legal cooperation.

events.name: Magdeburg Christmas Market Incident
events.enhanced_description: On December 20, 2024, a tragic incident occurred in Magdeburg, Germany, when a car was driven into a crowd at a Christmas market, resulting in five deaths and 235 injuries. This attack raised concerns about public safety during festive events.

events.name: Teófilo Otoni Traffic Collision
events.enhanced_description: On December 21, 2024, a multiple-vehicle collision on the BR-116 highway in Teófilo Otoni, Brazil, resulted in 41 deaths and seven injuries, marking it as the deadliest traffic accident on federal highways in Brazil since monitoring began in 2007.

events.name: 2025 Catholic Church Jubilee
events.enhanced_description: On December 24, 2024, the Catholic Church commenced the 2025 Jubilee, a significant event in the Church's calendar that celebrates faith and renewal among its followers worldwide.

events.name: Azerbaijan Airlines Flight 8243 Crash
events.enhanced_description: On December 25, 2024, Azerbaijan Airlines Flight 8243, an Embraer ERJ-190AR, crashed near Aktau International Airport in Kazakhstan, with 29 of the 67 passengers surviving. This incident raised concerns over aviation safety in the region.

events.name: Han Duck-soo Impeachment
events.enhanced_description: On December 27, 2024, Acting President Han Duck-soo was impeached by members of the National Assembly for failing to promulgate two bills related to President Yoon's legal proceedings. He was succeeded by Deputy Prime Minister Choi Sang-mok, marking a significant political shift.

events.name: Jeju Air Flight 2216 Crash

locations.name: Muan International Airport, Muan, South Korea

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, Jeju Air Flight 2216, a Boeing 737-800, crashed at Muan International Airport after veering off the runway, resulting in the tragic deaths of 179 people. The incident raised serious concerns about aviation safety and emergency response protocols in South Korea.

events.name: political crisis: Michel Barnier loses a motion of no-confidence
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, Michel Barnier became the first French Prime Minister to lose a motion of no-confidence since Georges Pompidou in 1962, marking a significant political crisis in France. This event highlighted the growing discontent with Barnier's administration and raised questions about the stability of his government.

events.name: Brian Thompson assassination

locations.name: Metropolitan Museum of Art
locations.historical_name: Bacchanal: A Faun Teased by Children

events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, Brian Thompson, the CEO of UnitedHealthcare, was shot and killed by a lone gunman in Midtown Manhattan. This tragic event sparked widespread debate and criticism regarding the health insurance industry in the United States, raising concerns about safety and corporate governance.

events.name: John Mahama elected president
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, John Mahama of the National Democratic Congress (NDC) was elected president of Ghana for a second non-consecutive term. His return to power was seen as a pivotal moment in Ghana's political landscape, reflecting the electorate's desire for continuity and change.

events.name: Notre-Dame Cathedral reopens
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, the Notre-Dame Cathedral in Paris reopened to the public after extensive renovations following a devastating fire in 2019. This reopening marked a significant cultural milestone for France, symbolizing resilience and the restoration of one of the world's most iconic landmarks.

events.name: Mikheil Kavelashvili elected unopposed
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, Mikheil Kavelashvili of the People's Power party was elected unopposed as president of Georgia. His election without opposition raised questions about the political landscape in Georgia and the future of democratic processes in the country.

events.name: Yoon Suk Yeol impeached
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, South Korean President Yoon Suk Yeol faced impeachment as members of parliament voted to suspend his powers and duties following his controversial declaration of martial law. This event underscored the political tensions in South Korea and the challenges facing Yoon's administration.

events.name: Cyclone Chido strikes Mayotte
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, Cyclone Chido made landfall in Mayotte, resulting in at least 172 deaths and widespread devastation across the island. The disaster prompted urgent humanitarian responses and highlighted the vulnerabilities of island communities to extreme weather events.

events.name: Political asylum granted to Marcin Romanowski
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, the Hungarian government, led by Prime Minister Viktor Orbán, granted political asylum to Polish MP Marcin Romanowski, who was wanted on an European Arrest Warrant for alleged fraud. This decision raised significant political implications regarding Hungary's stance on EU laws and asylum policies.

events.name: Mazan rapes trial verdict
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, the Judicial Court in Avignon found Dominique Pelicot guilty of the aggravated rape of his ex-wife, Gisèle Pelicot, sentencing him to the maximum of 20 years in prison. This case, involving multiple defendants, highlighted serious issues surrounding domestic violence and legal accountability in France.

events.name: Jubilee in the Catholic Church begins
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, a Jubilee year began in the Catholic Church, a time of special significance marked by celebrations, pilgrimages, and spiritual renewal. This event is part of the Church's tradition of offering indulgences and promoting reconciliation among its followers.

events.name: Parker Solar Probe sets record
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, the Parker Solar Probe broke its own record for the closest artificial object to the Sun, surpassing the previous record set in 2018 by 6.1 million kilometers. This achievement marked a significant milestone in solar research and our understanding of the Sun's atmosphere.

events.name: Truck accident in Ethiopia
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 2024, a truck carrying passengers fell off a bridge over the Ganale Doria River in Bona Zuria, Sidama Region, Ethiopia, resulting in the deaths of 71 people and injuring 4 others. This tragic accident highlighted ongoing issues related to road safety and infrastructure in the region.

events.name: The Epiphany Rising
events.enhanced_description: The Epiphany Rising was a failed rebellion in England aimed at restoring the deposed King Richard II. The uprising was quickly suppressed, resulting in the execution of several nobles involved, including the Earl of Salisbury and the Earl of Kent.

events.name: Death of Richard II
events.enhanced_description: Richard II, the deposed King of England, died under mysterious circumstances in Pontefract Castle, likely ordered by King Henry IV to prevent any potential uprisings. His death marked the end of a tumultuous period in English history.

events.name: Henry Percy (Hotspur) incursions into Scotland
events.enhanced_description: In February 1400, Henry Percy, known as Hotspur, led incursions into Scotland, marking a period of conflict between England and Scotland. These military actions were part of the ongoing tensions that characterized the Hundred Years' War.

events.name: Abdication of Trần Thiếu Đế
events.enhanced_description: Five-year-old Trần Thiếu Đế was forced to abdicate the throne of Đại Việt in favor of his maternal grandfather, Hồ Quý Ly, marking the end of the Trần dynasty after 175 years and the beginning of the Hồ dynasty.

events.name: Sir Thomas Percy resigns as Admiral
events.enhanced_description: Sir Thomas Percy, 1st Earl of Worcester, resigned from his position as Admiral of the North and West to join the resistance against King Henry IV. His resignation signified a growing discontent among the nobility during this turbulent period.

events.name: Installation of Alexandru cel Bun
events.enhanced_description: Alexandru cel Bun was installed as the new Prince of Moldavia by Mircea the Elder after the removal of the reigning monarch, Prince Iuga. This event marked a significant shift in the leadership of Moldavia during a time of regional instability.

events.name: Battle of Baigou River
events.enhanced_description: During the Jingnan campaign, Zhu Di, Prince of Yan, achieved a decisive victory against the Imperial forces led by General Li Jinglong at the Battle of Baigou River. The battle was notable for the chaos caused by a sudden gust of wind that disrupted the Imperial flag.

events.name: Death of King Swa Saw Ke
events.enhanced_description: King Swa Saw Ke of Ava died after a lengthy reign of 33 years, leading to the ascension of his son, King Tarabya. However, Tarabya's reign was short-lived, lasting less than seven months before he was assassinated.

events.name: Meeting of Prince-electors in Frankfurt
events.enhanced_description: In a significant political maneuver, three prince-electors of the Holy Roman Empire convened in Frankfurt to discuss the deposition of Emperor Wenceslaus due to his ineffective leadership. They ultimately selected Frederick I, Duke of Brunswick-Lüneburg, as a potential replacement.

events.name: Assassination of Frederick I of Brunswick-Lüneburg
events.enhanced_description: Frederick I of Brunswick-Lüneburg was assassinated shortly after being identified as a rival to Emperor Wenceslaus. His assassination occurred while he was returning from a meeting of the prince-electors, highlighting the intense political rivalries of the time.

events.name: Envoy of King Robert III crosses into England
events.enhanced_description: Sir John Swinton, an envoy of King Robert III of Scotland, crossed into England with a group of knights under a writ of safe conduct from King Henry IV. This diplomatic mission aimed to negotiate peace during a tense period between the two kingdoms.

events.name: Re-establishment of Jagiellonian University
events.enhanced_description: Jagiellonian University was re-established in Kraków by order of King Władysław II, marking a significant moment in the history of education in Poland. The creation of the Faculty of Theology was partly funded by the sale of jewelry from the late Queen Jadwiga.

events.name: Demand from King Henry IV to King Robert III
events.enhanced_description: King Henry IV of England sent a formal demand to King Robert III of Scotland, insisting on a meeting to discuss the obligations of Scotland to England. This demand was made against the backdrop of ongoing tensions between the two kingdoms.

events.name: Henry IV leads army into Scotland
events.enhanced_description: After receiving no response from King Robert III, King Henry IV led the English army into Scotland, reaching Haddington and then Leith. This military campaign was part of the ongoing conflict between England and Scotland.

events.name: Meeting at Lahneck Castle
events.enhanced_description: At Lahneck Castle, the princes of the German states convened to vote on the deposition of Holy Roman Emperor Wenceslaus due to his ineffective leadership. This meeting reflected the growing discontent among the nobility regarding the Emperor's rule.

events.name: Election of Rupert as King of the Romans
figures: Rupert, Count Palatine of the Rhine
events.enhanced_description: Rupert, Count Palatine of the Rhine, was elected as King of the Romans, a significant event in the political landscape of the Holy Roman Empire. His election was part of the broader efforts to stabilize the Empire amidst internal conflicts.

events.name: Henry IV returns to England
events.enhanced_description: After failing to secure a pledge of fealty from King Robert III of Scotland, King Henry IV returned to England. This retreat marked a setback in his attempts to assert English dominance over Scotland.

events.name: Proclamation of Owain Glyndŵr
events.enhanced_description: Owain Glyndŵr was proclaimed Prince of Wales by his followers, initiating a series of attacks on English strongholds in northeast Wales. This marked the beginning of a significant Welsh uprising against English rule.

events.name: Tamerlane's stop at Behesna
events.enhanced_description: Tamerlane, the Mongol conqueror, halted at the Turkish garrison in Behesna during his campaign. After an initial provocation, he launched a successful attack that led to the surrender of the garrison.

events.name: Capture of Cangzhou
events.enhanced_description: During the Jingnan campaign, Prince Zhu Di of Yan captured Cangzhou in Hebei province, further expanding his conquests. This victory was part of his broader efforts to assert control over the Ming dynasty.

events.name: Destruction of Aleppo
events.enhanced_description: Tamerlane initiated the destruction of Aleppo, overwhelming the defenders from the Mamluk Sultanate. This brutal campaign resulted in significant loss of life and marked a pivotal moment in the region's history.

events.name: Surrender of Aleppo
events.enhanced_description: The Mamluk Sultanate surrendered the city of Aleppo to Tamerlane's forces, leading to a massacre of many inhabitants. This event underscored Tamerlane's ruthless military strategy and the fragility of Mamluk power.

events.name: Ascension of Minkhaung I
events.enhanced_description: Minkhaung I ascended to the throne of Ava following a power struggle that ensued after the assassination of King Tarabya. His rise marked a new chapter in the history of the largest kingdom in northern Myanmar.

events.name: Visit of Manuel II Palaiologos to England
events.enhanced_description: Manuel II Palaiologos became the only Byzantine Emperor to visit England, where he was warmly received by King Henry IV at Blackheath. This visit occurred during the Christmas holiday and highlighted the diplomatic relations between the Byzantine Empire and England.

events.name: Battle of Dongchang
events.enhanced_description: In a significant setback during the Jingnan campaign, Prince Zhu Di's forces faced a serious defeat at the Battle of Dongchang, where they were encircled by Imperial General Sheng Yong. Despite the loss, Zhu Di managed to escape and regroup for future engagements.

events.name: Timur defeats both the Ottoman Empire and the Mamluk Sultanate of Egypt, to capture the city of Damascus in present-day Syria
events.enhanced_description: In 1401, Timur, the Turko-Mongol conqueror, successfully captured Damascus after defeating both the Ottoman Empire and the Mamluk Sultanate. Following the conquest, his troops committed widespread massacres against the city's inhabitants, marking a brutal chapter in the region's history.

events.name: Timur conquers the Empire of The Black Sheep Turkomans, in present-day Azerbaijan, and the Jalayirid dynasty in present-day Iraq
events.enhanced_description: In 1401, Timur launched a campaign against the Black Sheep Turkomans and the Jalayirid dynasty, successfully conquering their territories in present-day Azerbaijan and Iraq. The rulers Qara Yusuf and Sultan Ahmad fled to seek refuge with the Ottoman Sultan Bayezid I, marking a significant shift in power in the region.

events.name: In modern-day Korea, King Jeongjong of Joseon abdicates in fear of an attack by his ambitious younger brother, Taejong
events.enhanced_description: In 1401, King Jeongjong of the Joseon Dynasty abdicated the throne due to fears of an impending attack from his younger brother, Taejong, who was known for his ambition. This event marked a significant power shift within the royal family and set the stage for Taejong's eventual ascension to the throne.

events.name: Prince Parameswara establishes the Malacca Sultanate, in present-day western Malaysia and northern Sumatra
events.enhanced_description: In 1401, Prince Parameswara founded the Malacca Sultanate, which would become a significant trading empire in Southeast Asia. This establishment marked the beginning of a powerful maritime kingdom that played a crucial role in regional trade and cultural exchange.

events.name: Hananchi succeeds Min as King of Hokuzan, in modern-day north Okinawa, Japan
events.enhanced_description: In 1401, Hananchi ascended to the throne as the King of Hokuzan, succeeding Min. This transition marked a significant moment in the history of the Ryukyu Kingdom, which would later play a vital role in regional politics and trade.

events.name: Wallachia (modern-day southern Romania) resists an invasion by the Ottomans
events.enhanced_description: In 1401, the principality of Wallachia successfully resisted an invasion by the Ottoman Empire, showcasing the military prowess of its ruler, Mircea the Elder. This resistance was a significant event in the ongoing struggle between the Ottomans and the Balkan states.

events.name: A Wallachian army captures Iuga, and makes Alexandru cel Bun the Prince of Moldavia
events.enhanced_description: In 1401, a Wallachian army captured the strategic location of Iuga, leading to the appointment of Alexandru cel Bun as the Prince of Moldavia. This event was pivotal in shaping the political landscape of the region during this period.

events.name: The Kingdom of Kongo begins
events.enhanced_description: In 1401, the Kingdom of Kongo was established in Central Africa, marking the rise of one of the most powerful and influential kingdoms in the region. This kingdom would play a significant role in trade and cultural exchanges between Africa and Europe.

events.name: The Haast's eagle and Moa are both driven to extinction by Māori hunters
events.enhanced_description: Around 1401, the Haast's eagle and Moa, two iconic species of New Zealand, were driven to extinction largely due to hunting by the Māori people. This event highlights the impact of human activity on biodiversity in isolated ecosystems.

events.name: The Mississippian culture starts to decline
events.enhanced_description: In 1401, the Mississippian culture, known for its complex societies and mound-building, began to experience a decline. This decline was attributed to various factors, including environmental changes and social upheaval.

events.name: Europe is reported to have around 52 million inhabitants
events.enhanced_description: In 1401, it was estimated that Europe had a population of approximately 52 million inhabitants. This demographic data provides insight into the social and economic conditions of the continent during the late medieval period.

events.name: The House of Medici becomes powerful in Florence
events.enhanced_description: In 1401, the House of Medici began to rise in power within Florence, establishing themselves as a dominant political and cultural force. Their influence would shape the Renaissance and the development of art and politics in Italy.

events.name: Newcastle upon Tyne is created a county corporate, by Henry IV of England

locations.name: Newcastle upon Tyne, Tyne and Wear

coordinate_source.cache_key: Newcastle upon Tyne, Tyne and Wear

events.enhanced_description: In 1401, Newcastle upon Tyne was granted the status of a county corporate by King Henry IV of England. This designation allowed the city to govern itself and marked an important step in its development as a significant urban center.

events.name: Jean Froissart completes his Chronicles, detailing the events of the 14th Century in France
events.enhanced_description: In 1401, the chronicler Jean Froissart completed his seminal work, 'Chronicles,' which provided a detailed account of the events of the 14th century in France. His writings are considered a crucial source for understanding medieval history.

events.name: Rupert, King of Germany, is crowned King of the Romans at Cologne
events.enhanced_description: On January 6, 1401, Rupert of Germany was crowned King of the Romans in Cologne, solidifying his claim to the imperial title within the Holy Roman Empire. This event was significant in the context of the political struggles of the time.

events.name: Emperor Hồ Quý Ly of Dai Ngu (now Vietnam) passes the throne to his son, Hồ Hán Thương
events.enhanced_description: On January 12, 1401, Emperor Hồ Quý Ly of Dai Ngu abdicated the throne in favor of his son, Hồ Hán Thương. This transition marked a significant moment in the history of Vietnam, as it reflected the dynastic changes of the period.

events.name: After their disastrous defeat on December 25 in the Battle of Dongchang in the Jingnan campaign, the forces of the Principality of Yan within China return to Beiping (located at the site of present-day Beijing)
events.enhanced_description: On January 16, 1401, following a significant defeat in the Battle of Dongchang during the Jingnan campaign, the forces of the Principality of Yan retreated to Beiping, present-day Beijing. This event was part of a larger power struggle within the Ming dynasty.

events.name: The Parliament of England is opened at Westminster by King Henry IV
events.enhanced_description: On January 20, 1401, King Henry IV opened a session of the Parliament of England at Westminster. This event was significant in the context of the political landscape of England during the early 15th century.

events.name: The Byzantine Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos accepts a payment of 3,000 English gold marks in support of an alliance between England and Byzantium
events.enhanced_description: On February 3, 1401, Byzantine Emperor Manuel II Palaiologos, after spending time in England, accepted a payment of 3,000 English gold marks from King Henry IV. This financial support was aimed at strengthening the alliance between England and the Byzantine Empire.

events.name: William Sawtrey becomes the first person in England to be burned at the stake under the new De heretico comburendo law
events.enhanced_description: On March 2, 1401, William Sawtrey, a Roman Catholic priest and Lollard, was burned at the stake in Smithfield, London, becoming the first victim of the De heretico comburendo law. This event marked a significant moment in the history of religious persecution in England.

events.name: King Henry IV gives royal assent to the Suppression of Heresy Act
events.enhanced_description: On March 10, 1401, King Henry IV of England granted royal assent to the Suppression of Heresy Act, which allowed secular authorities to punish religious crimes. This act was influenced by the Archbishop of Canterbury and targeted the Lollards, followers of John Wycliffe.

events.name: The Samogitians rebel against the Teutonic knights and burn two castles
events.enhanced_description: On March 13, 1401, the Samogitians, supported by Grand Duke Vytautas of Lithuania, rebelled against the Teutonic Knights, successfully burning two of their castles. This rebellion was part of the ongoing conflicts between the Teutonic Order and the local populations.

events.name: Jingnan campaign
events.enhanced_description: The Jingnan campaign was a pivotal military conflict during the Ming dynasty, where Prince Zhu Di mobilized his forces from Beijing to challenge the Jianwen Emperor. This campaign marked the beginning of Zhu Di's efforts to claim the throne, leading to significant political upheaval within the dynasty.

events.name: Appointment of John Barry
events.enhanced_description: In 1401, John Barry was appointed as the new Attorney-General for Ireland, a significant role in the governance of the country during a time of political strife and conflict. His appointment reflected the ongoing struggles for power and legal authority in Ireland.

events.name: Capture of Conwy Castle
events.enhanced_description: On Good Friday in 1401, Conwy Castle was captured through cunning tactics by Welsh brothers Rhys and Gwilym ap Tudur, supporting the rebellion led by Owain Glyndŵr against English rule. This event was a significant moment in the Welsh struggle for independence.

events.name: Imprisonment of King Zsigmond
events.enhanced_description: King Zsigmond of Hungary was taken prisoner on April 28, 1401, after refusing to comply with demands from Archbishop John Kanizsai and Palatine Derek Bebek. His imprisonment highlighted the political tensions and struggles for power within the kingdom.

events.name: Law prohibiting private use of the Bucentaur
events.enhanced_description: On May 6, 1401, the council of the Republic of Venice enacted a law to prevent the Doge from using the state-owned ship, the Bucentaur, for private purposes. This legislation was part of broader efforts to maintain the integrity of state resources.

events.name: Death of Maria, Queen of Sicily
events.enhanced_description: Maria, Queen of Sicily, passed away on May 25, 1401, after a reign of nearly 34 years. Her death marked a significant transition in the political landscape of Sicily, impacting the region's governance and alliances.

events.name: Laurence Allerthorp becomes Lord High Treasurer
events.enhanced_description: On May 31, 1401, Laurence Allerthorp was appointed as the new Lord High Treasurer of England, succeeding Sir John Norbury. This position was crucial for managing the kingdom's finances during a period of political instability.

events.name: Destruction of food supplies at Dezhou
events.enhanced_description: On June 15, 1401, during the Jingnan campaign, rebel Yan forces destroyed food supplies belonging to the Ming Chinese government at Dezhou. This act was part of a broader strategy to weaken the imperial forces and assert control over the region.

events.name: Mission dispatched to Ming China
events.enhanced_description: On June 24, 1401, Shogun Ashikaga Yoshimitsu dispatched a mission to Ming Dynasty China, marking a significant step towards establishing trade relations between the two nations. This diplomatic effort was crucial for fostering economic and cultural exchanges.

events.name: Schaffhausen massacre
events.enhanced_description: On June 25, 1401, the Schaffhausen massacre resulted in the brutal killing of 30 Jewish residents, following the murder of a young boy named Konrad Lori. This tragic event highlighted the rampant anti-Semitism and violence against Jewish communities in medieval Europe.

events.name: Reduction of the English Pale
events.enhanced_description: In June 1401, the English Pale in Ireland was significantly reduced to include only Dublin, County Kildare, County Louth, and County Meath. This contraction reflected the declining influence of English rule in Ireland amidst growing local resistance.

events.name: Timur's raid on Baghdad
events.enhanced_description: On July 9, 1401, Timur launched a brutal raid on Baghdad, resulting in a massacre of its inhabitants as punishment for their resistance. This event was marked by horrific violence, with reports of tens of thousands killed and the city left in ruins.

events.name: Raid on Beiping
events.enhanced_description: On July 15, 1401, Chinese imperial troops led by Fang Zhao launched a raid on the Yan principality's capital at Beiping, forcing Prince Zhu Di to retreat north. This confrontation was part of the larger Jingnan campaign, which sought to consolidate imperial power.

events.name: End of the County of Geneva
events.enhanced_description: On August 5, 1401, the County of Geneva was sold to Amadeus VIII, Count of Savoy, marking the end of its independence after over 300 years. This transaction significantly altered the political landscape of the region.

events.name: Yan principality defeats Chinese forces
events.enhanced_description: On September 18, 1401, the Yan principality achieved a significant victory over Chinese imperial forces at Beiping after a prolonged siege. This battle was a crucial moment in the Jingnan campaign, showcasing the resilience of Zhu Di's forces.

events.name: Canonization of John Twenge
events.enhanced_description: On September 24, 1401, the late cleric John Twenge was canonized as Saint John of Bridlington by Pope Boniface IX. This canonization reflected the growing veneration of saints in medieval Christianity and the influence of the papacy.

events.name: Restoration of Sultan Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah Tughluq
events.enhanced_description: On October 14, 1401, Sultan Nasir-ud-Din Mahmud Shah Tughluq was restored to power in Delhi, marking a significant moment in the tumultuous history of the Delhi Sultanate. His return to the throne was pivotal in stabilizing the region after a period of unrest.

events.name: Release of King Zsigmond
events.enhanced_description: On October 29, 1401, King Zsigmond of Hungary was released from imprisonment by order of the Royal Council, allowing him to resume his rule. His release was a critical turning point in the political dynamics of Hungary during this period.

events.name: Battle of Tuthill
events.enhanced_description: On November 2, 1401, the Battle of Tuthill occurred at Caernarfon, where Owain Glyndŵr's forces faced a significant defeat, losing 300 soldiers to the English Army. This battle marked the first display of Glyndŵr's banner, The Golden Dragon, symbolizing his resistance against English rule.

events.name: Zhu Di's military campaign

locations.name: Yangtze River, near Nanjing, Jiangsu, China

events.enhanced_description: On December 2, 1401, during the Jingnan campaign, Zhu Di adopted a new military strategy, moving southward from Beiping to the Yangtze River and capturing several key locations including Dong'e, Dongping, Wenshang, and Pei. This shift in tactics was crucial for his campaign against the Ming dynasty.

events.name: Establishment of the Malwa Sultanate
events.enhanced_description: In 1401, Dilawar Khan established the Malwa Sultanate in present-day northern India, marking the rise of a new political entity in the region. This development was significant in the context of the fragmented political landscape of India during this period.

events.name: Tributary relationship of Joseon with Ming
events.enhanced_description: In 1401, the Joseon dynasty in present-day Korea officially entered into a tributary relationship with Ming dynasty China, solidifying diplomatic and trade ties between the two nations. This relationship was pivotal for Korea's political and cultural development.

events.name: Japan re-enters tributary relationship with China
events.enhanced_description: In 1401, Japan re-entered into a tributary relationship with Ming dynasty China, marking a significant diplomatic shift. This relationship facilitated trade and cultural exchanges, influencing both nations' interactions.

events.name: Marriage of King Jogaila
events.enhanced_description: On January 29, 1402, King Jogaila of the Poland–Lithuania Union married Anna of Celje, a strategic alliance aimed at consolidating his rule and addressing dissent against his authority in Poland. This marriage was significant for the political landscape of Eastern Europe.

events.name: Observation of the Great Comet of 1402
events.enhanced_description: In early February 1402, the Great Comet was first observed in the Northern Hemisphere, captivating the attention of people across various regions. Visible for eight days, it became a significant astronomical event, influencing cultural interpretations and scientific inquiries.

events.name: Unsuccessful raid on Jihlava
events.enhanced_description: On February 19, 1402, Sigismund of Křižanov, Prokop of Luxemburg, and King Wenceslas IV of Bohemia led an unsuccessful raid against the military garrison of Jihlava, targeting the Kingdom of Croatia. The raid ended in defeat, resulting in the capture of Wenceslas IV.

events.name: Death of David Stewart, Duke of Rothesay
events.enhanced_description: On March 26, 1402, David Stewart, Duke of Rothesay and heir to the Scottish throne, died while imprisoned by his uncle, Robert Stewart, 1st Duke of Albany. His death raised suspicions of foul play and intensified the power struggle within the Scottish nobility.

events.name: Yan Army reaches Suishui
events.enhanced_description: On April 2, 1402, during the Jingnan campaign, the Yan Army, led by Prince Zhu Di, reached Suishui, located west of Huaibei in present-day Anhui province. This marked a significant advance in their military campaign against the Imperial forces of Southern China.

events.name: Marriage by proxy of Henry IV and Joan of Navarre
events.enhanced_description: On April 3, 1402, King Henry IV of England was married by proxy to Joan of Navarre in a ceremony held at Eltham Palace near London. This marriage was politically significant, strengthening ties between England and Navarre.

events.name: Yan Army overwhelms Imperial Army at Linghi
events.enhanced_description: On April 29, 1402, during the Jingnan campaign, the Yan Army led by Zhu Di decisively defeated the Imperial Army of Southern China at Linghi, capturing General Ping An. This victory further solidified Zhu Di's position in the conflict.

events.name: Yan Army captures Sixian
events.enhanced_description: On May 7, 1402, the Yan Army continued its advance during the Jingnan campaign, capturing Sixian and reaching the north bank of the Huai River. This strategic movement brought them closer to the Imperial capital.

events.name: Marriage of Martin I of Sicily and Blanche of Navarre
events.enhanced_description: On May 21, 1402, following the death of Queen Maria of Sicily, her husband Martin I married Blanche of Navarre by proxy. This union was significant for the political landscape of the region.

events.name: Yan Army crosses Yangtze River

locations.name: Yangtze River, near Nanjing, Jiangsu, China

events.enhanced_description: On June 3, 1402, the Yan Army, after crossing the Huai River and capturing Yangzhou and Luhe, crossed the Yangtze River at Guazhou. This maneuver brought them within striking distance of the Imperial capital, Nanjing.

events.name: Yan Army surrounds Nanjing
events.enhanced_description: On June 13, 1402, the Yan Army arrived at the walls of Nanjing, the capital of Imperial China, and surrounded the city. The defenders opened the gates, leading to a tragic end for Emperor Zhu Yun Wen and his court.

events.name: Zhu Di becomes Emperor Yongle
events.enhanced_description: On June 14, 1402, Zhu Di, the King of the Yan State, was proclaimed the new Ming Dynasty Emperor Yongle in Nanjing, marking a significant unification of northern and southern China under his rule.

events.name: Battle of Casalecchio
events.enhanced_description: On June 26, 1402, the Battle of Casalecchio occurred, where Gian Galeazzo Visconti, the Duke of Milan, crushed the forces of Bologna and Florence. This victory solidified Visconti's power in Northern Italy.

events.name: Battle of Bryn Glas

locations.name: Bryn Glas, Powys, Wales, United Kingdom

events.enhanced_description: In 1402, the Battle of Bryn Glas saw Welsh rebels under Owain Glyndŵr defeat the English on the England/Wales border. The Welsh captured Edmund Mortimer, a significant figure who later married Glyndŵr's daughter.

events.name: Crowning of Zhu Di as Emperor Yongle
events.enhanced_description: On July 17, 1402, Zhu Di was formally crowned as the new Ming Dynasty Emperor Yongle in Nanjing, marking the conclusion of the Jingnan campaign and the beginning of a new era in Chinese history.

events.name: Battle of Ankara
