events.name: First Peace of Thorn
events.enhanced_description: On February 1, 1411, the First Peace of Thorn was signed, concluding the Polish–Lithuanian–Teutonic War. The treaty resulted in the Teutonic Knights ceding Dobrzyń Land to the Kingdom of Poland, reshaping the balance of power in the region.

events.name: Parliament in Calatayud
events.enhanced_description: On February 8, 1411, a parliament convened in Calatayud, Spain, to elect a successor to the recently deceased King Martin of Aragon. Despite nominations, the parliament failed to reach a consensus on a new king, leading to a political impasse.

events.name: Death of Süleyman Çelebi
events.enhanced_description: On February 17, 1411, Sultan Süleyman Çelebi was strangled to death after being forced to flee Edirne by his brother Musa Çelebi. This event marked a significant turning point in the Ottoman Interregnum, leading to Musa's ascension.

events.name: Foundation of Ahmedabad
events.enhanced_description: On February 26, 1411, Ahmad Shah I laid the foundation of Ahmedabad at the site of Asawal, marking the establishment of a city that would become a major center of trade and culture in India.

events.name: Friso-Hollandic Wars: Capture of Staveren
events.enhanced_description: During the Friso-Hollandic Wars, Friesland soldiers captured the city of Staveren, the last stronghold in Friesland, after a harsh winter prevented both sides from crossing the Zuiderzee. This event marked a significant shift in control during the conflict.

events.name: Gujarat Sultan Ahmen Shah I declares the new city of Ahmedabad to be the new Gujarat capital
events.enhanced_description: In 1411, Sultan Ahmen Shah I declared Ahmedabad as the new capital of Gujarat, marking a significant shift in the political landscape of the region. This decision not only established Ahmedabad as a center of power but also initiated its development into a major urban hub.

events.name: Carlo I Tocco arrives at Ioannina in Greece to become the new ruler of the former Byzantine state, the Despotate of Epirus
events.enhanced_description: In April 1411, Carlo I Tocco arrived in Ioannina to assume control over the Despotate of Epirus, a former Byzantine territory. His rule marked a continuation of the complex political dynamics in the region following the decline of Byzantine authority.

events.name: Sandalj Hranić sells Ostrovica to the Republic of Venice
events.enhanced_description: On April 13, 1411, Sandalj Hranić, Duke of Bosnia, sold the coastal town of Ostrovica to the Republic of Venice. This transaction significantly enhanced Venetian control over the Dalmatian coast and solidified their maritime dominance in the Adriatic Sea.

events.name: Battle of Roccasecca
events.enhanced_description: On May 19, 1411, General Muzio Attendolo, under the command of Louis II of Anjou, achieved a decisive victory against King Ladislaus of Naples at the Battle of Roccasecca. This battle was a crucial moment in the ongoing power struggles in Italy during the early 15th century.

events.name: Friedrich IV becomes Duke of Further Austria
events.enhanced_description: On June 3, 1411, Friedrich IV, known as 'Friedrich of the Empty Pockets', ascended to the title of Duke of Further Austria following the death of his brother, Leopold the Fat. His reign would be marked by the challenges of managing the diverse territories of the Habsburgs.

events.name: Roquefort cheese rights granted
events.enhanced_description: On June 4, 1411, King Charles VI of France granted exclusive rights to the city of Roquefort-sur-Soulzon for the ripening and marketing of Roquefort cheese. This decree helped establish the region's reputation for producing this renowned cheese.

events.name: Zheng He returns to Nanjing
events.enhanced_description: On July 6, 1411, Admiral Zheng He returned to Nanjing after his second voyage, bringing with him the Sinhalese king, who had been captured during the Ming–Kotte War. This event underscored the Ming Dynasty's naval prowess and its expanding influence in the Indian Ocean.

events.name: Sigismund elected King of the Romans
events.enhanced_description: On July 21, 1411, Sigismund was unanimously elected as King of the Romans by the seven electors of the Holy Roman Empire. His election was a pivotal moment in the governance of the empire, which faced numerous challenges during his reign.

events.name: Battle of Harlaw
events.enhanced_description: On July 24, 1411, the Battle of Harlaw took place in Scotland, where Domhnall of Islay, Lord of the Isles, faced off against an army commanded by Alexander Stewart, Earl of Mar. The battle ended in a bloody draw, highlighting the ongoing conflicts over control in the Scottish Highlands.

events.name: Parameswara of Malacca hosted by Ming Court
events.enhanced_description: On August 4, 1411, Parameswara of Malacca, also known as Iskandar Shah, was hosted by the Ming Court in Nanjing for a series of banquets. This visit marked a significant diplomatic engagement between the Malay Sultanate and the Ming Dynasty.

events.name: Treaty of Selymbria concluded
events.enhanced_description: On September 3, 1411, the Treaty of Selymbria was concluded between the Ottoman Empire and the Republic of Venice, marking a significant diplomatic agreement that shaped the balance of power in the region.

events.name: King Henry IV calls ninth parliament
events.enhanced_description: On September 21, 1411, King Henry IV of England summoned his ninth parliament, a crucial assembly that would address various political issues of the time, including governance and taxation.

events.name: Negotiations at Abbey of St Vaast
events.enhanced_description: On October 3, 1411, John the Fearless, Duke of Burgundy, hosted negotiations at the Abbey of St Vaast in Arras with English Bishop Henry Chichele and envoys regarding English support in the French civil war. The discussions ultimately failed to secure significant backing.

events.name: Duke of Burgundy captures Paris
events.enhanced_description: On October 22, 1411, the Duke of Burgundy, with the assistance of English mercenaries, successfully captured Paris. This event marked a significant turning point in the ongoing conflicts during the French civil war.

events.name: English Parliament assembles
events.enhanced_description: On November 3, 1411, the English Parliament was convened by King Henry IV, during which Thomas Chaucer was elected as Speaker of the House of Commons. This assembly was significant for addressing the governance of the kingdom.

events.name: Appenzell enters alliance with Swiss Confederacy
events.enhanced_description: On November 24, 1411, the Swiss canton of Appenzell entered into an alliance with most of the cantons of the Swiss Confederacy. This alliance strengthened the political unity and military cooperation among the Swiss regions.

events.name: Henry IV dismisses Prince Henry
events.enhanced_description: On November 30, 1411, King Henry IV dismissed Prince Henry and his supporters from the government, a move that reflected the ongoing tensions within the English court and the struggle for power.

events.name: Royal assent to acts passed by Parliament
events.enhanced_description: On December 19, 1411, King Henry IV granted royal assent to numerous acts passed by the English Parliament, including the Riot Act 1411, which aimed to address civil disorder and maintain peace.

events.name: Henry IV issues pardons to Welsh rebels
events.enhanced_description: On December 21, 1411, King Henry IV of England issued pardons to nearly all Welsh rebels involved in the Glyndŵr rebellion, sparing only the leaders Owain Glyndŵr and Thomas of Trumpington. This act was part of the ongoing efforts to stabilize relations with Wales.

events.name: Work begins on Grand Canal restoration
events.enhanced_description: In 1411, under the Yongle Emperor of the Ming Dynasty, extensive work began to restore the ancient Grand Canal of China, which had fallen into disrepair during the Yuan dynasty. This monumental project involved thousands of laborers and aimed to enhance trade and transportation.

events.name: Constantinople besieged by Musa Çelebi
events.enhanced_description: In 1411, Constantinople was briefly besieged by the Ottoman pretender Musa Çelebi, who sought to reclaim power during the Ottoman Interregnum. The siege was a reflection of the internal strife within the Ottoman Empire and the city's strategic importance.

events.name: Battle of İnceğiz
events.enhanced_description: Possibly in early 1412, the Battle of İnceğiz occurred between the rival brothers Mehmed Çelebi and Musa Çelebi during the Ottoman Interregnum. This conflict was part of the broader struggle for control of the Ottoman Empire.

events.name: Medici Family made bankers of the Papacy
events.enhanced_description: On January 16, 1412, the Medici Family was officially appointed as the bankers of the Papacy, solidifying their financial influence and power in Renaissance Italy. This role would enable them to play a crucial part in the politics and culture of the time.

events.name: Ernest marries Cymburgis of Masovia
events.enhanced_description: On January 25, 1412, Ernest, Duke of Austria, married Cymburgis of Masovia. This marriage was significant for strengthening political alliances in Central Europe during a period of territorial disputes.

events.name: Mining Code enacted in Serbia
events.enhanced_description: On January 29, 1412, the 'Mining Code' (Zakon o Rudnishma) was enacted in Serbia by Despot Stefan Lazarević to regulate mineral extraction. This legislation aimed to promote responsible mining practices and economic development in the region.

events.name: The Alcañiz Concord
events.enhanced_description: The Alcañiz Concord was a pivotal agreement reached in the city of Alcañiz, where nine delegates were selected to choose a new, undisputed King of Aragon. This event was crucial in resolving the succession crisis following the death of King Martin of Aragon.

events.name: Battle of Morvedre
events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Morvedre was fought in the Kingdom of Valencia, where supporters of Ferdinand of Antequera clashed with those loyal to James II, Count of Urgell. This battle was a significant moment in the power struggle for the throne of Aragon.

events.name: Charter of the University of St Andrews

locations.name: St Andrews, Fife, Scotland, United Kingdom

events.enhanced_description: The University of St Andrews, one of the oldest universities in the English-speaking world, was granted a charter of privilege by the local bishop in 1412. This charter marked a significant step in the establishment of higher education in Scotland.

events.name: Compromise of Caspe
events.enhanced_description: The Compromise of Caspe was a crucial agreement reached in the town of Caspe, where nine delegates were chosen to resolve the succession crisis following the death of King Martin of Aragon. This led to the election of Ferdinand of Antequera as the new King of Aragon.

events.name: Duke Albert V becomes Duke of Mecklenburg
events.enhanced_description: Upon the death of his father, Duke Albert IV, Albert V ascended to the title of Duke of Mecklenburg. This transition marked a significant moment in the history of the region as it continued the lineage of the House of Mecklenburg.

events.name: Installation of Abu’l-Fa’dl Abbas Al-Musta'in
events.enhanced_description: In Cairo, Abu’l-Fa’dl Abbas Al-Musta'in was installed as the Sultan of Egypt by rebels, serving as a temporary replacement for his father, Sultan An-Nasir Faraj. His rule lasted only six months before he returned to his role as Caliph.

events.name: Assassination of Gian Maria Visconti
events.enhanced_description: Gian Maria Visconti, the Duke of Milan, was assassinated in front of the church of San Gottardo by Milanese Ghibellines on the orders of his rival, Facino Cane. This event marked a significant shift in power within the city.

events.name: Treaty of Bourges
events.enhanced_description: The Treaty of Bourges was signed between King Henry IV of England and Charles, Duke of Orléans, granting England full sovereignty over Aquitaine and Gascony in exchange for military support against the Burgundians. This treaty was a significant diplomatic maneuver during the Hundred Years' War.

events.name: Assassination of An-Nasir Faraj
events.enhanced_description: An-Nasir Faraj, the Mamluk Sultan of Egypt and Syria, was assassinated in Damascus after surrendering to the Emirs of Syria. His death led to a power vacuum in the region, with his son being confirmed as the ruler of Egypt.

events.name: Agreement between Antipope John XXIII and King Ladislaus of Naples
events.enhanced_description: Antipope John XXIII signed an agreement with King Ladislaus of Naples, investing him with the Neapolitan crown in exchange for military support against Pope Benedict XII. This agreement highlighted the complex interplay between religion and politics during this period.

events.name: Ferdinand of Antequera proclaimed King of Aragon
events.enhanced_description: Ferdinand of Antequera was officially proclaimed King of Aragon by delegates in Caspe, following a two-year succession crisis that began with the death of King Martin. This event solidified his claim to the throne and marked a new chapter in Aragonese history.

events.name: Proclamation of Ferdinand I as King of Aragon
events.enhanced_description: As the Compromise of Caspe was read aloud by Friar Vicent Ferrer, Ferdinand I was proclaimed King of Aragon by the delegates. This proclamation marked the end of a contentious succession crisis and established Ferdinand's rule.

events.name: Behnam Hadloyo becomes Patriarch
events.enhanced_description: Behnam Hadloyo was appointed as the Syriac Orthodox Patriarch of Mardin, a significant religious leadership position within the Syriac Orthodox Church. His leadership would influence the Christian community in the region.

events.name: Peace of Auxerre
events.enhanced_description: The Peace of Auxerre was signed between the Duchy of Burgundy and the Armagnacs, arranging a marriage between Philip, Count of Vertus, and Catherine of Burgundy. Although the marriage never took place, this agreement aimed to solidify political alliances.

events.name: Battle of Motta
events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Motta was fought when the Republic of Venice faced an invasion by a coalition of Hungarians, Germans, and Croats. The Venetian forces achieved a decisive victory, inflicting heavy casualties on the invading army.

events.name: Ferdinand I declared Count of Barcelona
events.enhanced_description: Ferdinand I of Aragon was declared Count of Barcelona, a title that further solidified his political power in the region. This declaration was part of his broader efforts to unify the crowns of Aragon and Castile.

events.name: Accession of Emperor Shoko
events.enhanced_description: Emperor Go-Komatsu abdicated the throne, leading to the accession of Emperor Shoko in Japan. This transition was part of the complex political landscape of the Nanboku-chō period, characterized by rival imperial lines.

events.name: Eric of Pomerania becomes sole ruler of the Kalmar Union
events.enhanced_description: Following the death of Queen Margaret, Eric of Pomerania became the sole ruler of the Kalmar Union, which united Sweden, Denmark, and Norway. His reign would be marked by challenges in maintaining the union's stability.

events.name: Al-Mu'ayyad Shaykh becomes Mamluk Sultan
events.enhanced_description: Al-Mu'ayyad Shaykh forced Sultan Al-Musta'in to abdicate, becoming the new Mamluk Sultan of Egypt. This power shift was indicative of the turbulent political climate in the region during this period.

events.name: Ava–Hanthawaddy War
events.enhanced_description: During the Ava–Hanthawaddy War, King Razadarit of Hanthawaddy led an invasion of Prome with a force of 4,000 troops. This conflict was part of the ongoing struggle for dominance in the region of modern-day Myanmar.

events.name: Final summons of the English Parliament by Henry IV
events.enhanced_description: King Henry IV of England issued a summons for the English Parliament for the last time, directing the members of Commons and the House of Lords to assemble. This event marked the end of his active involvement in parliamentary affairs.

events.name: Ming treasure voyages ordered by Yongle Emperor
events.enhanced_description: The Yongle Emperor of China ordered the fourth of the Ming treasure voyages, to be led by Admiral Zheng He. These voyages were significant for establishing Chinese maritime power and expanding trade networks across the Indian Ocean.

events.name: Battle of Chalagan
events.enhanced_description: In December, the Battle of Chalagan saw the Kara Koyunlu Turkomans defeat the Georgians led by Constantine I and their ally Ibrahim I of Shirvan. This battle was part of the ongoing conflicts in the region during the early 15th century.

events.name: Jousting tournament in Buda
events.enhanced_description: The first mention of Wallachian knights competing in a jousting tournament took place in Buda, highlighting the cultural exchange and the popularity of chivalric tournaments in medieval Europe.

events.name: Valladolid laws declared by John II of Castile
events.enhanced_description: John II of Castile declared the Valladolid laws, which restricted the social rights of Jews, including forcing them to wear distinctive clothing and barring them from administrative positions. This legislation reflected the growing anti-Semitic sentiments in medieval Spain.

events.name: Jiao Yu adds preface to Huolongjing
events.enhanced_description: In 1412, Jiao Yu, a prominent artillery officer of the Ming Dynasty, added a preface to his seminal work, the Huolongjing, which detailed advancements in gunpowder warfare and artillery technology. This work significantly influenced military tactics and technology in China and beyond.

events.name: The Black Death sweeps England for a final time
events.enhanced_description: The Black Death, which ravaged Europe in the 14th century, returned to England for a final wave around 1412, exacerbating the already dire social and economic conditions. This pandemic led to significant population loss and social upheaval across the country.

events.name: End of the First Scutari War
events.enhanced_description: The First Scutari War, fought between the Kingdom of Zeta and the Venetian Republic, concluded on January 30, 1413. This conflict was part of the broader struggle for control over the Adriatic region and highlighted the tensions between local powers and Venetian interests.

events.name: Opening of the 10th Parliament of King Henry IV
events.enhanced_description: On February 3, 1413, the 10th and final Parliament of King Henry IV convened in Westminster. However, it was short-lived, closing after six weeks due to the king's declining health and eventual death.

events.name: Death of King Henry IV of England
events.enhanced_description: King Henry IV of England passed away on March 20, 1413, at Westminster Abbey, where Parliament was in session. His death marked the end of a tumultuous reign and set the stage for the ascension of his son, Henry V.

events.name: Henry V ascends to the throne
events.enhanced_description: On March 21, 1413, Henry, Prince of Wales, was proclaimed King Henry V of England, following the death of his father, Henry IV. His ascension marked the beginning of a new era in English history, characterized by military campaigns in France.

events.name: Henry V summons Parliament
events.enhanced_description: King Henry V summoned the English Parliament to convene at Westminster on March 22, 1413, as part of his efforts to consolidate power and address pressing national issues following his recent ascension to the throne.

events.name: Genoa regains independence
events.enhanced_description: On March 27, 1413, the Republic of Genoa regained its independence from French control, electing Giorgio Adorno as Doge for life. This marked a significant shift in power dynamics in the region and the restoration of local governance.

events.name: Surrender of Dai Viet to China
events.enhanced_description: On March 31, 1413, Trung Quang De, the Emperor of Dai Viet (modern-day Vietnam), surrendered his kingdom to Chinese control. This event marked the beginning of a period of Chinese domination over Vietnam.

events.name: Coronation of Henry V
events.enhanced_description: The coronation of Henry V as King of England took place on April 9, 1413, at Westminster Abbey. This ceremony solidified his claim to the throne and marked the beginning of his reign, which would be characterized by military campaigns in France.

events.name: Cabochien revolt begins
events.enhanced_description: On April 27, 1413, the Cabochien revolt erupted in Paris, led by Simon Caboche, as rebels seized the Bastille prison and took the Provost of Paris, Pierre des Essarts, hostage. This uprising reflected the growing discontent among the populace against the ruling elite.

events.name: First Parliament of Henry V assembles
events.enhanced_description: The first Parliament of King Henry V convened at Westminster on May 14, 1413, shortly after his coronation. This assembly was crucial for addressing the pressing issues of the kingdom and establishing Henry's authority.

events.name: Ordonnance cabochienne signed
events.enhanced_description: On May 22, 1413, amidst the turmoil of the Cabochien revolt, King Charles VI of France enacted the 'Ordonnance cabochienne,' which limited his royal powers. This law was a response to the growing unrest and highlighted the challenges faced by the monarchy.

events.name: Ali Shah Miri becomes Sultan of Kashmir
events.enhanced_description: On May 31, 1413, Ali Shah Miri ascended to the throne as the new Sultan of Kashmir, following the death of his father, Sultan Sikandar Shah Miri. His reign would be marked by the challenges of governance in a region with a rich cultural heritage.

events.name: Ladislaus of Naples sacks Rome
events.enhanced_description: On June 8, 1413, King Ladislaus of Naples led his troops to conquer and sack the city of Rome, driving out Antipope John XXIII. This event underscored the political instability in Italy during this period and the ongoing power struggles among various factions.

events.name: Parliament closes in England
events.enhanced_description: On June 9, 1413, the English Parliament concluded its session, with King Henry V granting royal assent to several acts, including the Corn Measure Act and the Parliamentary Elections Act. These laws were significant for regulating elections and agricultural practices.

events.name: Ludwig becomes Landgrave of Hesse
events.enhanced_description: On June 10, 1413, Ludwig ascended to the throne as the new Landgrave of Hesse following the death of his father, Hermann II. His reign would play a crucial role in the political landscape of the German principalities.

events.name: Battle of Çamurlu
events.enhanced_description: On July 5, 1413, the Battle of Çamurlu took place, where Mehmed I defeated his brother Musa, effectively ending the Ottoman Interregnum. This victory solidified Mehmed's position as the Sultan and marked a significant moment in Ottoman history.

events.name: End of the Cabochien revolt
events.enhanced_description: The Cabochien revolt in Paris came to an end on August 3, 1413, as the citizenry and nobles rose against the rebel control. The aftermath saw the execution of many Cabochiens, while key leaders managed to escape, highlighting the volatility of the period.

events.name: University of St Andrews chartered
events.enhanced_description: On August 28, 1413, the University of St Andrews in Scotland was chartered by papal bull, establishing it as one of the oldest universities in the English-speaking world. This event marked a significant development in higher education in Scotland.

events.name: Repeal of the Ordonnance cabochienne
events.enhanced_description: On September 5, 1413, the French government repealed the 'Ordonnance cabochienne,' restoring the powers of King Charles VI. This repeal was a response to the political turmoil and the need to stabilize royal authority.

events.name: Union of Horodło signed
events.enhanced_description: On October 2, 1413, the Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania signed the Union of Horodło, strengthening their political alliance. This agreement was pivotal in shaping the future of both nations and their regional influence.

events.name: Tewodros I ascends the throne of Ethiopia
events.enhanced_description: On October 12, 1413, Tewodros I ascended to the throne as Emperor of Ethiopia following the death of his father, Dawit I. His reign would be marked by efforts to modernize the empire and strengthen its central authority.

events.name: Renewal of alliance between Brandenburg and Pomerania-Wolgast
events.enhanced_description: On November 19, 1413, the Margraviate of Brandenburg renewed its alliance with the Duchy of Pomerania-Wolgast against the Duchy of Pomerania-Stettin. This alliance was significant in the context of regional power struggles in Northern Europe.

events.name: Henry V summons Parliament to assemble
events.enhanced_description: On December 1, 1413, King Henry V of England summoned Parliament to assemble on April 30 at Westminster. This call to Parliament was part of his strategy to address governance and military matters following his recent coronation.

events.name: Reinterment of King Richard II
events.enhanced_description: On December 4, 1413, King Henry V of England ordered the remains of his predecessor, King Richard II, to be moved from King's Langley Priory to Westminster Abbey, a significant act of reconciliation and respect for the former monarch whom Henry's father had overthrown. This reinterment underscored the importance of Westminster Abbey as the traditional burial site for English monarchs.

events.name: Betrothal of Prince Charles of France
events.enhanced_description: On December 18, 1413, the betrothal ceremony of Prince Charles of France to Marie of Anjou took place at the Palais du Louvre in Paris. This union was politically significant as it aimed to strengthen alliances between the French royal family and the powerful Anjou dynasty.

events.name: Death of Michele Steno
events.enhanced_description: Michele Steno's rule as the Doge of Venice came to an end with his death on December 26, 1413, after 26 years in office. He was succeeded by Tommaso Mocenigo, marking a significant transition in the leadership of the Venetian Republic.

events.name: Christianization of Samogitia
events.enhanced_description: In 1413, Samogitia became the last region in Europe to be Christianized, marking a significant milestone in the spread of Christianity across the continent. This event reflected the broader religious transformations occurring during this period.

events.name: Beginning of the Annals of the Joseon Dynasty
events.enhanced_description: The Annals of the Joseon Dynasty, a crucial historical record of Korea, began in 1413. These annals provide a detailed account of the political, social, and cultural history of the Joseon period, which lasted for several centuries.

events.name: Michael Küchmeister von Sternberg becomes Grand Master
events.enhanced_description: On January 7, 1414, Michael Küchmeister von Sternberg was appointed as the 28th Grand Master of the Teutonic Order, succeeding Heinrich von Plauen. His leadership would influence the Order's military and political strategies in the region.

events.name: Oldcastle Revolt
events.enhanced_description: The Oldcastle Revolt began on January 9, 1414, led by John Oldcastle, as an uprising by the Lollards against King Henry V. The rebellion was quickly suppressed by Henry's forces, resulting in the capture and execution of many rebels.

events.name: Coronation of Ferdinand I as King of Aragon
events.enhanced_description: Ferdinand I was crowned King of Aragon on February 11, 1414, in Zaragoza. This event marked a significant moment in the history of the Crown of Aragon, as Ferdinand's reign would influence the political landscape of the region.

events.name: Burning of Jean Petit's Speech
events.enhanced_description: On February 26, 1414, the speech of French theologian Jean Petit was publicly burned in Paris by order of the inquisitor Gerard de Montaigu. This act highlighted the tensions between emerging reformist ideas and established religious authorities during this period.

events.name: Abu’l-Faḍl Abbas Al-Musta'in forced out as Caliph
events.enhanced_description: On March 9, 1414, Abu’l-Faḍl Abbas Al-Musta'in was ousted from his position as Caliph of Cairo, following his earlier abdication as Sultan of Egypt. This power shift was orchestrated by Sultan Al-Mu'ayyad Shaykh, who appointed his brother as the new Caliph.

events.name: End of Tran Quy Khoang's Rebellion
events.enhanced_description: The rebellion led by Vietnamese Emperor Tran Quy Khoang against the Ming dynasty came to an end on March 30, 1414, when he was captured by General Zhang Fu. This marked a significant turning point in the ongoing Ming–Vietnamese conflict.

events.name: Yongle Emperor's Campaign against Oirat Mongols
events.enhanced_description: On April 6, 1414, the Yongle Emperor of China departed from Beijing to lead a military campaign against the Oirat Mongols. This campaign was part of his broader efforts to consolidate power and expand the Ming dynasty's influence.

events.name: Second English Parliament of Henry V
events.enhanced_description: The second English Parliament of King Henry V opened on April 30, 1414, in Westminster, where Walter Hungerford was elected as Speaker of the House of Commons. This session was significant for the legislative developments that occurred during Henry's reign.

events.name: Khizr Khan conquers Delhi Sultanate
events.enhanced_description: On May 28, 1414, Khizr Khan, the governor of Multan under Timur, successfully conquered the Delhi Sultanate from Daulat Khan Lodi, establishing the Sayyid Dynasty. This event marked a significant shift in power within the Indian subcontinent.

events.name: Yeshaq I becomes Emperor of Ethiopia
events.enhanced_description: On June 23, 1414, Yeshaq I succeeded his brother Tewodros I as Emperor of Ethiopia. His ascension marked a continuation of the Solomonic dynasty's influence in the region.

events.name: Capture of Iskandar Mirza
events.enhanced_description: On July 21, 1414, Iskandar Mirza, who had ruled the Timurid Empire since 1409, was captured as the city of Isfahan surrendered to Shah Rukh. This event marked a significant turning point in the power dynamics of the Timurid Empire.

events.name: Joanna II becomes Queen of Naples
events.enhanced_description: On August 6, 1414, Joanna II ascended to the throne as the reigning Queen of Naples following the death of her brother, King Ladislaus. Her reign would be marked by political intrigue and challenges to her authority.

events.name: Foundation of the Sancta dels Folls
events.enhanced_description: On August 29, 1414, the brotherhood of the Sancta dels Folls Dona Nostra i Desamparats Innocents was founded in Valencia to assist the mentally ill and later expanded its mission to care for homeless and abandoned children. This organization played a significant role in social welfare during its time.

events.name: Presentation of a Giraffe to Yongle Emperor
events.enhanced_description: On September 20, 1414, a giraffe was presented to China's Yongle Emperor as a gift from the Sultan of Bengal, Saifuddin Hamza Shah. This event symbolized the diplomatic relations and cultural exchanges between the Ming dynasty and South Asian kingdoms.

events.name: Jan Hus departs for the Council of Constance
events.enhanced_description: On October 8, 1414, the Bohemian church reformer Jan Hus left his home at the invitation of King Sigismund of Germany to attend the Council of Constance. Unfortunately, upon his arrival, he was imprisoned, leading to his eventual execution.

events.name: Coronation of Sigismund of Luxembourg
events.enhanced_description: On November 8, 1414, Sigismund of Luxembourg was crowned as King of the Romans at Aachen, four years after his election. This event was significant in the context of the Holy Roman Empire and its political dynamics.

events.name: Opening of the Council of Constance
events.enhanced_description: The Council of Constance opened on November 16, 1414, summoned by King Sigismund to resolve the Western Schism, which had seen three different Popes recognized by various factions. This council aimed to restore unity within the Catholic Church.

events.name: Third Parliament of Henry V
events.enhanced_description: The Third Parliament of King Henry V opened on November 19, 1414, in Westminster, where significant laws were passed, including the Suppression of Heresy Act and the Riot Act. This session reflected Henry's efforts to consolidate power and address social issues.

events.name: Completion of Ahmed Shah's Mosque
events.enhanced_description: On December 17, 1414, the construction of Ahmed Shah's Mosque in Ahmedabad was completed, with the date etched into stone. This mosque is a significant example of Indo-Islamic architecture and reflects the cultural heritage of the region.

events.name: Casimir, Duke of Oświęcim takes full power
events.enhanced_description: On December 19, 1414, Casimir officially assumes full power as Duke of Oświęcim upon reaching the age of 18, marking a significant transition in leadership for the region.

events.name: Ernest, Duke of Austria adopts the title of Archduke
events.enhanced_description: On January 1, 1414, Ernest, Duke of Austria, becomes the last duke to be enthroned in Carinthia through the ancient Carantanian ritual at the Prince's Stone, subsequently adopting the title of Archduke.

events.name: Suppression of Alien Priory Cells in England
events.enhanced_description: In 1414, the Alien Priory Cells, which were foreign monastic establishments in England, are suppressed, reflecting the growing tensions and nationalistic sentiments during this period.

events.name: Je Tsongkhapa declines Yongle Emperor's invitation
events.enhanced_description: In 1414, the prominent Tibetan lama Je Tsongkhapa declines an invitation from the Yongle Emperor to appear in Nanjing, sending instead his disciple Chosrje Shākya Yeshe, who is honored with the title 'State Teacher'.

events.name: Durham School founded
events.enhanced_description: In 1414, Durham School is established as a grammar school by Thomas Langley, Prince-Bishop of Durham, and continues to thrive as an independent institution over 600 years later.

events.name: Truce extended in the Burgundian War
events.enhanced_description: On January 24, 1415, representatives from England, including the Bishops of Durham and Norwich, meet with King Charles VI of France to extend the truce in the ongoing Burgundian War until May 1.

events.name: Battle of Dala
events.enhanced_description: On March 13, 1415, the decisive Battle of Dala occurs in Myanmar, where Crown Prince Minye Kyawswa of Ava leads his forces against King Razadarit of Hanthawaddy. Despite his valiant efforts, Minye Kyawswa is killed, but his troops ultimately defeat the invaders.

events.name: Antipope John XXIII's escape
events.enhanced_description: On March 20, 1415, Antipope John XXIII escapes from Constance, taking refuge in Schaffhausen, in the Duchy of Austria, despite his earlier promise to resign from his claims to the papacy.

events.name: Giorgio Adorno resigns as Doge of Genoa
events.enhanced_description: On March 23, 1415, Giorgio Adorno resigns as the Doge of Genoa, despite having been appointed for life, indicating the political instability of the time.

events.name: Barnaba Guano elected as Doge of Genoa
events.enhanced_description: On March 29, 1415, Barnaba Guano is elected as the new Doge of the Republic of Genoa, succeeding Giorgio Adorno amidst a backdrop of political change.

events.name: Razadarit authorizes invasion plan
events.enhanced_description: In early 1415, Razadarit, the ruler of the Hanthawaddy Kingdom, authorizes a plan to invade the forces of Minkhaung I of the Ava Kingdom, marking a significant escalation in the Forty Years' War.

events.name: Treaty of Arras signed
events.enhanced_description: In 1415, King Charles VI of France and John the Fearless, Duke of Burgundy, sign the Treaty of Arras, a pivotal agreement aimed at stabilizing the region amidst ongoing conflicts.

events.name: Haec sancta synodus decree approved
events.enhanced_description: On April 6, 1415, the Council of Constance approves the decree Haec sancta synodus, establishing the principle that an ecumenical council holds authority over the Pope in matters of faith.

events.name: Frederick I becomes Elector of Brandenburg
events.enhanced_description: On April 30, 1415, Frederick I is appointed as the Elector of Brandenburg, a significant position in the Holy Roman Empire that enhances his political influence.

events.name: Council of Constance condemns John Wycliffe
events.enhanced_description: On May 4, 1415, the Council of Constance declares John Wycliffe a heretic, banning his writings and ordering the removal of his remains from consecrated ground, reflecting the church's efforts to suppress dissent.

events.name: Antipope Benedict XIII issues prohibitions against Jews
events.enhanced_description: On May 11, 1415, Antipope Benedict XIII issues a papal bull from Valencia, imposing eleven prohibitions against Jews, including restrictions on education and public interaction, reflecting the era's pervasive anti-Semitism.

events.name: Council of Constance dismisses Antipope John XXIII
events.enhanced_description: On May 29, 1415, the Council of Constance formally dismisses Antipope John XXIII from any authority over the Roman Catholic Church, a critical step in resolving the Western Schism.

events.name: Jan Hus condemned and executed
events.enhanced_description: On June 5, 1415, Jan Hus is condemned by the Council of Constance for heresy and is subsequently executed by burning at the stake, marking a pivotal moment in the pre-Reformation movement.

events.name: Pope Gregory XII opens the Council of Constance
events.enhanced_description: On July 4, 1415, Pope Gregory XII officially opens the Council of Constance, where he later abdicates, becoming the last pope to resign until Pope Benedict XVI in 2013.

events.name: Jan Hus burned at the stake
events.enhanced_description: On July 6, 1415, Jan Hus is executed by burning at the stake in Konstanz, a significant event that highlights the tensions between reformist ideas and the established church.

events.name: Sigismund's trip to Perpignan
events.enhanced_description: On July 18, 1415, Sigismund, King of the Romans, departs from the Council of Constance to Perpignan, aiming to secure the resignation of Antipope Benedict XIII and to negotiate peace in ongoing conflicts.

events.name: Henry V informed of Southampton Plot
events.enhanced_description: On July 31, 1415, King Henry V of England learns of the Southampton Plot against him, leading to the arrest and execution of the conspirators before he launches his invasion of France.

events.name: Sigismund meets with Antipope Benedict XIII
events.enhanced_description: On September 20, 1415, Sigismund, King of the Germans, met with Antipope Benedict XIII in Avignon in an effort to persuade him to resign. This meeting was part of Sigismund's broader efforts to resolve the Great Western Schism, which had divided the Catholic Church.

events.name: Battle of Agincourt
events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Agincourt, fought on October 25, 1415, saw the English army, led by King Henry V, achieve a decisive victory against a much larger French force. The battle is particularly noted for the effectiveness of English longbowmen, which played a crucial role in the defeat of the French knights.

events.name: Opening of the English Parliament by Henry V
events.enhanced_description: On November 4, 1415, King Henry V opened the English Parliament for an 8-day session, a significant event in the governance of England during the Hundred Years' War. This session would address various matters of state, including military funding and legislation.

events.name: Marriage pledge between Brandenburg and Pomerania
events.enhanced_description: On November 5, 1415, Frederick I, Elector of Brandenburg, pledged his 3-year-old daughter Magdalene to Wartislaw IX, the 15-year-old Duke of Pomerania-Wolgast, in an attempt to resolve ongoing conflicts between their territories. This political maneuver aimed to secure peace through dynastic marriage.

events.name: Closure of the English Parliament after passing the Money Act
events.enhanced_description: The English Parliament was closed on November 12, 1415, after successfully passing the Money Act 1415, which increased penalties for the importation of illegal currency. This act was part of Henry V's broader efforts to stabilize the economy during wartime.

events.name: Treaty of Eberswalde
events.enhanced_description: On December 16, 1415, the Treaty of Eberswalde was signed between the duchies of Pomerania-Stettin and Brandenburg, temporarily ending the Uckermark War. The treaty involved territorial concessions in exchange for financial compensation, marking a significant diplomatic resolution.

events.name: Jean de Touraine becomes Dauphin of France
events.enhanced_description: On December 18, 1415, Jean de Touraine was named the new Dauphin of France following the death of his older brother, Louis, Duke of Guyenne. This succession was crucial for the French royal lineage during a tumultuous period marked by the Hundred Years' War.

events.name: Benedict XIII orders Talmuds to be delivered
events.enhanced_description: In January 1415, Pope Benedict XIII issued an order for all Talmuds to be delivered to the diocese, where they would be held until further notice. This action reflected the tensions between the Catholic Church and Jewish communities during this period.

events.name: Swiss Confederation takes Aargau
events.enhanced_description: In 1415, the Swiss Confederation successfully took control of the territory of Aargau from the House of Habsburg. This event marked a significant expansion of Swiss territory and influence during the early 15th century.

events.name: Restoration of the Grand Canal of China
events.enhanced_description: By 1415, the Grand Canal of China was reinstated after a period of disuse, following restoration efforts that began in 1411. This project, initiated by the Yongle Emperor, aimed to enhance the grain shipment system to support the new capital at Beijing.

events.name: Republic of Ragusa outlaws slavery
events.enhanced_description: On January 27, 1416, the Republic of Ragusa became the first state in Europe to officially outlaw slavery. This progressive legislation marked a significant step towards human rights in the region.

events.name: Battle of Gallipoli
events.enhanced_description: On May 29, 1416, Venetian admiral Pietro Loredan achieved a significant victory at the Battle of Gallipoli, where he destroyed the Ottoman fleet. This battle was pivotal in establishing Venetian naval dominance in the region.

events.name: Burning of Jerome of Prague
events.enhanced_description: On May 30, 1416, Jerome of Prague was burned at the stake as a heretic by the Catholic Church in Konstanz. His execution was part of the broader conflict between the Church and the Hussite movement, which sought reform within the Church.

events.name: Destruction of Trezzo sull'Adda Bridge
events.enhanced_description: In 1416, the Trezzo sull'Adda Bridge, which was the longest arch bridge in the world at the time, was destroyed. This event marked a significant loss in architectural heritage during the early 15th century.

events.name: Completion of the Hussite Bible
events.enhanced_description: The Hussite Bible was completed in 1416 by translators Tamás Pécsi and Bálint Újlaki. This translation was significant for the Hussite movement, which sought to make the scriptures accessible to the common people.

events.name: Defeat of Genoese fleet by English
events.enhanced_description: On June 29, 1417, an English fleet led by the Earl of Huntingdon defeated a fleet of Genoese carracks, capturing their admiral, known as the 'Bastard of Bourbon.' This victory underscored the naval prowess of England during this period.

events.name: Deposition of Pope Benedict XIII
events.enhanced_description: On July 27, 1417, Pope Benedict XIII was deposed, effectively ending the Great Western Schism that had divided the Catholic Church for decades. His removal paved the way for the election of Pope Martin V, restoring unity to the Church.

events.name: Henry V begins using English in correspondence
events.enhanced_description: On August 12, 1417, King Henry V of England began using English in his correspondence while on campaign in France. This marked a significant cultural shift, as it was the first time English was used in official documents since the Norman Conquest.

events.name: Capture of Caen by Henry V
events.enhanced_description: On September 20, 1417, Henry V of England captured the city of Caen in Normandy, which would remain under English control until 1450. This victory was part of Henry's campaign to reclaim French territories during the Hundred Years' War.

events.name: Pope Martin V succeeds Gregory XII
events.enhanced_description: On November 14, 1417, Pope Martin V was elected as the 206th pope, succeeding Gregory XII, who had abdicated in 1415. His election marked the end of the Great Western Schism and the restoration of papal authority.

events.name: Earliest description of Tynwald Day
events.enhanced_description: In 1417, the earliest extant description of Tynwald Day, the annual meeting of the Isle of Man's parliament, was documented in law. This event is significant in the history of democratic governance in the Isle of Man.

events.name: First recorded use of street lighting in London
events.enhanced_description: In 1417, the use of street lighting was first recorded in London when Mayor Sir Henry Barton ordered lanterns with lights to be hung out during winter evenings. This initiative marked a significant advancement in urban infrastructure and public safety.

events.name: Mircea cel Bătrân loses Dobruja to the Ottomans
events.enhanced_description: In 1417, Mircea cel Bătrân lost the region of Dobruja to the Ottomans, leading to the payment of tribute to prevent Wallachia from becoming an Ottoman province. This event was significant in the context of Ottoman expansion in Eastern Europe.

events.name: Chimalpopoca succeeds Huitzilihuitl as Tlatoani
events.enhanced_description: In 1417, Chimalpopoca succeeded his father Huitzilihuitl as Tlatoani (monarch) of Tenochtitlan, the capital of the Aztec Empire. His reign would be marked by the challenges of maintaining power amidst growing external threats.

events.name: Succession of Michael I of Wallachia
events.enhanced_description: On January 31, 1418, Michael I succeeded Mircea I as the ruler of Wallachia. His ascension came during a period of significant political instability and external threats from the Ottoman Empire.

events.name: The Council of Constance ends
events.enhanced_description: The Council of Constance, which began in 1414, concluded on April 22, 1418, resolving significant issues within the Catholic Church, including the election of Pope Martin V and the condemnation of John Hus. This council was pivotal in addressing the Western Schism and reforming church practices.

events.name: John the Fearless, Duke of Burgundy, captures Paris
events.enhanced_description: On May 29, 1418, John the Fearless, Duke of Burgundy, successfully captured Paris, a critical stronghold during the ongoing conflicts of the Hundred Years' War. This event significantly shifted the balance of power in France, aligning the Burgundians with the English against the Armagnacs.

events.name: The English Siege of Rouen begins
events.enhanced_description: In July 1418, the English forces commenced the Siege of Rouen, a strategic city in Normandy, during the Hundred Years' War. The siege would last until 1419, culminating in the city's surrender and solidifying English control over Normandy.

events.name: King Taejong abdicates the throne
events.enhanced_description: On September 18, 1418, King Taejong of the Joseon dynasty abdicated the throne in favor of his son, Sejong the Great. This transition marked the beginning of a reign that would be noted for significant cultural and scientific advancements in Korea.

events.name: João Gonçalves Zarco leads one of the first Portuguese expeditions to the Madeira Islands
events.enhanced_description: In 1418, João Gonçalves Zarco led one of the first Portuguese expeditions to the Madeira Islands, marking a significant moment in the Age of Discovery. This expedition laid the groundwork for the Portuguese colonization and exploration of the Atlantic.

events.name: Hundred Years' War: Rouen surrenders to Henry V of England
events.enhanced_description: On January 19, 1419, Rouen surrendered to Henry V of England, marking a pivotal moment in the Hundred Years' War. This victory allowed the English to consolidate their control over Normandy, significantly impacting the course of the conflict.

events.name: The Ōei Invasion of Tsushima Island begins
events.enhanced_description: The Ōei Invasion of Tsushima Island commenced on June 20, 1419, when Joseon Korea launched an attack on this strategically important island. This invasion was part of broader conflicts between Korea and Japan during this period.

events.name: The first Defenestration of Prague occurs
events.enhanced_description: On July 30, 1419, the first Defenestration of Prague took place, where radical Hussites threw several members of the city council out of a window. This event marked the beginning of the Hussite Wars and was a significant moment in Bohemian history.

events.name: Siege of Ceuta: The Portuguese successfully defend against Moroccan invaders
events.enhanced_description: In August 1419, during the Siege of Ceuta, Portuguese forces successfully defended the city against Moroccan attempts to retake it. This victory was crucial for maintaining Portuguese control over the strategic port and marked a significant moment in the Reconquista.

events.name: John the Fearless is assassinated
events.enhanced_description: On September 10, 1419, John the Fearless, Duke of Burgundy, was assassinated by adherents of the Dauphin Charles during a meeting in Montereau. This assassination escalated the conflict between the Burgundians and Armagnacs, further destabilizing France.

events.name: The Ottoman–Venetian peace treaty is signed
events.enhanced_description: In November 1419, the Ottoman–Venetian peace treaty was signed, concluding four years of conflict. This treaty recognized Venetian possessions in the Aegean and the Balkans, stabilizing relations between the two powers.

events.name: Portuguese sea captains discover the Madeira Islands
events.enhanced_description: In 1419, Portuguese sea captains João Gonçalves Zarco and Tristão Vaz Teixeira, under the patronage of Prince Henry the Navigator, discovered the Madeira Islands. This discovery was significant for the expansion of Portuguese maritime exploration.

events.name: The University of Rostock is established
events.enhanced_description: In 1419, the University of Rostock was established, becoming the oldest university in northern Europe. This institution played a crucial role in the development of higher education in the region.

events.name: Mirza Shahrukh sends an embassy to China
events.enhanced_description: In 1419, Mirza Shahrukh, the Timurid ruler of Persia, sent a large embassy to the court of the Yongle Emperor in China. The envoy, Ghiyāth al-dīn Naqqāsh, documented his travels, providing valuable insights into Chinese society and culture.

events.name: Mihail I defends Wallachia against the Ottomans
events.enhanced_description: In 1419, Mihail I, the ruler of Wallachia, successfully defended his territory against Ottoman incursions with the assistance of Hungarian forces. This defense was crucial in maintaining Wallachia's autonomy during a period of Ottoman expansion.

events.name: Final 41 treasure ships are built in Nanjing
events.enhanced_description: In 1419, the final 41 treasure ships were constructed in the shipyards of Nanjing, intended for the expeditions of the famed admiral Zheng He. These ships played a key role in establishing maritime trade routes and diplomatic relations across the Indian Ocean.

events.name: The Çelebi Sultan Mehmed Mosque is inaugurated

locations.name: Didymoteicho, East Macedonia and Thrace, Greece

events.enhanced_description: In March 1420, the Çelebi Sultan Mehmed Mosque was inaugurated in Didymoteicho, showcasing the architectural style of the Ottoman Empire. This mosque served as a significant religious site in the region.

events.name: Treaty of Troyes is signed
events.enhanced_description: On May 21, 1420, the Treaty of Troyes was signed, recognizing Henry V of England as the heir to the French throne during a period of Burgundian dominance in France. This treaty aimed to solidify English claims and control over French territories.

events.name: Henry the Navigator is appointed Grand Master
events.enhanced_description: On May 25, 1420, Henry the Navigator was appointed Grand Master of the Military Order of Christ, a position that allowed him to further his ambitions in exploration and maritime trade. His leadership significantly influenced the Age of Discovery.

events.name: Catherine of Valois marries King Henry V of England
events.enhanced_description: On June 2, 1420, Catherine of Valois married King Henry V of England, a union that strengthened the ties between England and France amidst the ongoing Hundred Years' War. This marriage was politically significant, aiming to secure peace between the two nations.

events.name: Venetian troops capture Udine
events.enhanced_description: On June 7, 1420, troops of the Republic of Venice captured Udine after a prolonged siege, effectively ending the independence of the Patriarchal State of Friuli. This event marked a significant expansion of Venetian influence in the region.

events.name: Construction of the dome of Florence Cathedral begins
events.enhanced_description: On August 7, 1420, construction began on the dome of the Florence Cathedral, designed by Filippo Brunelleschi. This architectural feat would become a defining symbol of Renaissance architecture and a landmark in Florence.

events.name: A 9.4 magnitude earthquake shakes Chile
events.enhanced_description: On August 31, 1420, a powerful 9.4 magnitude earthquake struck the Atacama Region of Chile, causing widespread devastation and triggering tsunamis that affected coastal areas as far away as Hawaii and Japan.

events.name: Ghiyāth al-dīn Naqqāsh records his travels in China
events.enhanced_description: On October 22, 1420, Ghiyāth al-dīn Naqqāsh, an envoy from the Timurid ruler Mirza Shahrukh, documented his crossing of a remarkable floating pontoon bridge over the Yellow River in Lanzhou. His accounts provided valuable insights into the engineering and culture of Ming China.

events.name: Beijing designated as the capital of the Ming Dynasty
events.enhanced_description: On October 28, 1420, Beijing was officially designated as the capital of the Ming Dynasty, coinciding with the completion of the Forbidden City. This decision marked a significant shift in the political landscape of China.

events.name: Hussite Wars – Battle of Vyšehrad
events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Vyšehrad, fought on November 1, 1420, was a significant conflict during the Hussite Wars where Sigismund, Holy Roman Emperor, faced a decisive defeat. This battle marked a crucial moment in the Hussite resistance against the imperial forces, leading to Sigismund's ejection from Bohemia.

events.name: Construction of Grace Dieu
events.enhanced_description: In 1420, Henry V of England commenced the construction of the ship Grace Dieu, which would become one of the largest and most powerful warships of its time. This vessel represented the advancements in naval technology and the growing importance of maritime power during the Hundred Years' War.

events.name: Tang Saier's Rebellion
events.enhanced_description: In 1420, Tang Saier led a rebellion against the Ming dynasty, successfully capturing two cities before ultimately being defeated. Her uprising highlighted the social unrest and challenges faced by the Ming emperors during this period.

events.name: Construction of the Temple of Heaven
events.enhanced_description: The construction of the Temple of Heaven in Beijing began in 1420, symbolizing the Ming dynasty's architectural grandeur and religious significance. This site became a central place for imperial ceremonies, reflecting the deep connection between the emperor and the divine.

events.name: Struggle for the Throne of Wallachia
events.enhanced_description: In 1420, a power struggle for the throne of Wallachia erupted between Radu II Praznaglava, supported by the Ottomans, and Dan II, backed by Hungary. This conflict would last for seven years, resulting in multiple changes of power and significant political instability in the region.

events.name: Defense of Moldavia
events.enhanced_description: In 1420, Alexandru cel Bun defended Moldavia against the first incursion by Ottoman forces at Cetatea Albă. This battle was significant in establishing Moldavia's resistance against Ottoman expansion in Eastern Europe.

events.name: Capital Shift to Beijing
events.enhanced_description: On February 2, 1421, the Yongle Emperor officially shifted the Ming dynasty's capital from Nanjing to Beijing. This strategic move was aimed at consolidating power and enhancing the defense against potential invasions.

events.name: Ming Treasure Voyages
events.enhanced_description: On March 3, 1421, Zheng He received an imperial order from the Yongle Emperor to commence the Ming treasure voyages. These expeditions were significant for establishing Chinese maritime dominance and fostering diplomatic relations across the Indian Ocean.

events.name: Battle of Baugé
events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Baugé, fought on March 21, 1421, saw a small French force surprise and defeat a smaller English contingent led by Thomas, Duke of Clarence. This battle was a notable victory for the French during the Hundred Years' War.

events.name: Death of Mehmed I
events.enhanced_description: On May 26, 1421, Mehmed I, the Sultan of the Ottoman Empire, passed away and was succeeded by his son, Murad II. This transition marked a significant moment in Ottoman history as the empire continued to expand under Murad's leadership.

events.name: Sale of Estates by John III of Dampierre
events.enhanced_description: In 1421, John III of Dampierre, Marquis of Namur, sold his estates to Philip the Good, Duke of Burgundy. This transaction was significant in the context of Burgundian expansion and consolidation of power in the Low Countries.

events.name: First Patent Issued by Florence
events.enhanced_description: In 1421, the Republic of Florence issued its first patent, marking a significant development in intellectual property rights during the Renaissance. This initiative reflected the growing importance of innovation and protection of inventions in the burgeoning economy.

events.name: Portuguese Exploration under Henry the Navigator
events.enhanced_description: In 1421, Portuguese sailors sent by Henry the Navigator successfully crossed Cape Non, reaching as far as Cape Bojador. This expedition was part of the early stages of the Age of Discovery, expanding European knowledge of the African coast.

events.name: Foundation of Larabanga Mosque
events.enhanced_description: Traditionally dated to 1421, the Larabanga Mosque was founded in northern Ghana, becoming one of the oldest mosques in the country. This site is significant for its architectural style and its role in the spread of Islam in West Africa.

events.name: Hussite Wars – Battle of Německý Brod
events.enhanced_description: On January 10, 1422, during the Hussite Wars, the Hussites achieved a significant victory against an army of Royalist Crusaders at the Battle of Německý Brod. This battle further solidified the Hussite movement's resistance against external forces.

events.name: Siege of Meaux
events.enhanced_description: On March 21, 1422, during the Hundred Years' War, the Siege of Meaux concluded with the surrender of the city to English forces. This event was a critical moment in the ongoing conflict between England and France.

events.name: Ottoman Siege of Constantinople
events.enhanced_description: In June 1422, the Ottoman Sultan Murad II besieged Constantinople, a pivotal moment in the Ottoman Empire's expansion. However, the siege was ultimately broken off due to the rebellion of Küçük Mustafa, showcasing the internal challenges faced by the Ottomans.

events.name: End of Spanish Era in Portugal
events.enhanced_description: On August 22, 1422, the Kingdom of Portugal officially ceased the use of the Spanish era dating system. This change reflected Portugal's growing national identity and independence from Spanish influence.

events.name: Henry VI Becomes King of England
events.enhanced_description: On September 1, 1422, Henry VI ascended to the throne of England at just nine months old, marking the beginning of a tumultuous reign that would see the country embroiled in the Wars of the Roses. His youth and the political instability of the time would shape his rule.

events.name: Treaty of Melno
events.enhanced_description: On September 27, 1422, the Teutonic Knights signed the Treaty of Melno with the Kingdom of Poland and the Grand Duchy of Lithuania, concluding the brief Gollub War. This treaty established the Prussian-Lithuanian border, which remained unchanged until World War I.

events.name: Proclamation of Kings in France
events.enhanced_description: Following the death of King Charles VI of France on October 21, 1422, Henry VI of England was proclaimed King of France in Paris, while his maternal uncle, Charles, was proclaimed King Charles VII in Bourges. This division of claims to the French throne intensified the conflict between England and France.

events.name: Fall of the Bulgarian Empire
events.enhanced_description: In 1422, Ottoman forces overran the last domains of Constantine II of Bulgaria, leading to his death in exile and marking the end of the Bulgarian Empire. This event signified the consolidation of Ottoman power in the Balkans.

events.name: Population of Venice and Florence
events.enhanced_description: In 1422, Venice had a population of approximately 84,000, governed by a small elite of 200 men, while Florence had around 40,000 inhabitants ruled by 600 men. This demographic snapshot illustrates the political structures and social hierarchies of these influential Italian city-states during the Renaissance.

events.name: Merger of Saxon Territories
events.enhanced_description: On January 6, 1423, the Electorate of Saxony merged with the Margravate of Meissen and the Duchy of Saxe-Wittenberg, creating a more unified political entity. This merger was significant in the context of the Holy Roman Empire's political landscape.

events.name: Hundred Years War: The island of Tombelaine is taken by English forces
events.enhanced_description: During the Hundred Years War, English forces captured the strategic island of Tombelaine, located off the coast of Normandy, to establish a base for future attacks on the fortified Mont Saint-Michel. This maneuver was part of the larger conflict between England and France over territorial claims.

events.name: Battle of Salangpur
events.enhanced_description: After a failed siege of Salangpur, Ahmad Shah I of Gujarat was ambushed by Hushang Shah's forces while returning to Ahmedabad. Despite the surprise attack, Ahmad Shah I emerged victorious, allowing him to continue his journey back to the capital.

events.name: Treaty of Amiens
events.enhanced_description: The Treaty of Amiens was signed during the Hundred Years War, establishing a mutual defense agreement between the Duchy of Burgundy, the Duchy of Brittany, and the Kingdom of England. This treaty aimed to strengthen alliances against French aggression.

events.name: Election of Francesco Foscari as Doge of Venice
events.enhanced_description: Francesco Foscari was elected as the new Doge of the Republic of Venice following the death of Tommaso Mocenigo. Foscari's tenure would last 34 years, marked by significant political and military events in the Venetian Republic.

events.name: Battle of Hořice

locations.name: Hořice, Hradec Králové Region, Czech Republic

events.enhanced_description: In the Battle of Hořice, the Taborites, a faction of the Hussite movement, decisively defeated the Utraquists, showcasing the internal divisions within the Hussite forces. This battle was significant in the ongoing Hussite Wars, which were characterized by religious and political strife in Bohemia.

events.name: Abdication of Ashikaga Yoshimochi
events.enhanced_description: Ashikaga Yoshimochi abdicated as shogun of Japan, passing the title to his son, Ashikaga Yoshikazu. This transition marked a significant moment in the Ashikaga shogunate, which was characterized by political instability and power struggles.

events.name: Ratification of the Treaty of Melno
events.enhanced_description: The Treaty of Melno was ratified, officially ending the Gollub War between the Teutonic Order and the alliance of Poland and Lithuania. This treaty marked a significant step towards stabilizing relations in the region after years of conflict.

events.name: Byzantine–Ottoman Wars: Breakthrough of Hexamilion
events.enhanced_description: During the Byzantine–Ottoman Wars, Turakhan Beg, the Ottoman governor of Thessaly, successfully breached the Hexamilion wall after a two-day battle. This victory allowed Ottoman forces to ravage the Peloponnese Peninsula, furthering their territorial ambitions in Greece.

events.name: Return of Ahmad Shah I to Gujarat
events.enhanced_description: After a series of military engagements, Ahmad Shah I of Gujarat successfully returned to his capital, Ahmedabad, to reassume the throne. His return marked a consolidation of power after the challenges he faced during his reign.

events.name: Election of Antipope Clement VIII
events.enhanced_description: Gil Sánchez Muñoz y Carbón was elected as Antipope Clement VIII by bishops in Avignon, following the death of Antipope Benedict XIII. This election highlighted the ongoing schism within the Catholic Church, as Clement VIII's legitimacy was contested by the Roman Pope Martin V.

events.name: Papal Approval of the Treaty of Melno
events.enhanced_description: Pope Martin V officially approved the Treaty of Melno, which ended the Gollub War between the Teutonic Order and the Polish-Lithuanian alliance. This papal endorsement was crucial for legitimizing the treaty and stabilizing the region.

events.name: Battle of Cravant
events.enhanced_description: In the Battle of Cravant, the French army faced a significant defeat against the English and their Burgundian allies. This battle, fought on the banks of the River Yonne, was part of the ongoing conflicts of the Hundred Years War, showcasing the military prowess of the English forces.

events.name: Yongle Emperor's Campaign Against the Northern Yuan
events.enhanced_description: The Yongle Emperor launched his fourth military campaign against the Northern Yuan, a remnant of the Mongol Empire, in an effort to consolidate Ming control over northern territories. This campaign was part of the broader Ming efforts to secure their borders and assert dominance in the region.

events.name: Ascension of Ataullah Muhammad Shah I
events.enhanced_description: Ataullah Muhammad Shah I ascended to the throne as the Sultan of Kedah, Malaysia, following the death of his father, Sulaiman Shah I. His reign would last for 50 years, continuing the legacy of his father's rule.

events.name: Treaty of Sveti Srdj
events.enhanced_description: The Treaty of Sveti Srdj was signed to conclude the Second Scutari War between the Serbian Despotate and the Venetian Republic, resolving territorial disputes over Scutari and other regions previously held by the Venetians.

events.name: Battle of La Brossinière
events.enhanced_description: The Battle of La Brossinière was fought during the Hundred Years War, where an English force led by Sir John De la Pole was decisively defeated by the combined armies of France, Anjou, and Maine. The battle resulted in significant casualties for the English, marking a setback in their campaign.

events.name: Second Parliament of King Henry VI of England
events.enhanced_description: The Second Parliament of King Henry VI of England convened in London after being summoned on September 1. Under the leadership of John Russell, the House of Commons deliberated on various laws until its adjournment in February of the following year.

events.name: Giovanni Aurispa's Return to Venice
events.enhanced_description: After a two-year expedition to Byzantium, Giovanni Aurispa returned to Venice with the largest collection of Greek manuscripts ever assembled at that time, including 238 ancient texts. This significant acquisition contributed to the Renaissance's revival of classical knowledge in Europe.

events.name: Withdrawal of Hussite Army from Prague
events.enhanced_description: During the Hussite Wars, General Sigismund Korybut, commander of the Hussite Army, withdrew his troops from Prague following orders from Vytautas, Grand Duke of Lithuania, and Władysław II Jagiełło, King of Poland. This decision reflected the complex alliances and conflicts of the period.

events.name: Release of King James I of Scotland
events.enhanced_description: King James I of Scotland was released from captivity in England after 18 years, following a ransom treaty of £40,000 secured by Scottish hostages. His release marked a significant moment in Scottish history, as it allowed him to reclaim his throne and begin his reign.

events.name: Return of King James I to Scotland
events.enhanced_description: King James I returned to Scotland for the first time since his capture in 1406, escorted by nobles from both England and Scotland. This event symbolized the end of his long captivity and the restoration of his rule in Scotland.

events.name: Coronation of James I of Scotland
events.enhanced_description: The coronation of James I as King of Scotland took place at Scone Abbey, where he performed his first knighthood ceremony, honoring 18 prominent nobles. This event marked the formal beginning of his reign and his commitment to restoring order in Scotland.

events.name: Battle of L'Aquila
events.enhanced_description: In the Battle of L'Aquila, forces led by Jacopo Caldora and Micheletto Attendolo of the Kingdom of Naples defeated Braccio da Montone, who was fighting for Alfonso V of Aragon. This battle was part of the ongoing conflicts in Italy during the early 15th century.

events.name: Battle of Zagonara
events.enhanced_description: The Battle of Zagonara saw the Duchy of Milan's army, led by Duke Filippo Maria Visconti, defeat the Republic of Florence's forces under Carlo I Malatesta. This victory solidified Milan's power in Northern Italy during a tumultuous period.

events.name: Battle of Verneuil
events.enhanced_description: In the Battle of Verneuil, an English force led by John, Duke of Bedford, defeated a larger French army commanded by the Duke of Alençon, resulting in the capture of Alençon and the death of Archibald Douglas. This battle was a significant event in the ongoing Hundred Years' War.

events.name: Ascension of Emperor Renzong of Ming
events.enhanced_description: Prince Zhu Gaochi ascended to the throne as Emperor Renzong of the Ming dynasty following the death of his father, the Yongle Emperor. His reign marked the beginning of the Hongxi era, which aimed to restore stability after years of military campaigns.

events.name: Completion of the Bohemian Campaign
events.enhanced_description: The Bohemian campaign concluded with the signing of a treaty among the factions involved in the Hussite Wars, marking a significant moment in the conflict that had divided the region. This treaty aimed to bring peace and stability to Bohemia.

events.name: Hussite March to North Moravia
events.enhanced_description: Led by Jan Žižka, the Hussites began their march towards North Moravia to suppress a rebellion. This movement was part of the larger Hussite Wars, which were characterized by religious and political strife in Bohemia.

events.name: Prokop the Great Takes Command of the Hussites
events.enhanced_description: Following the death of Jan Žižka from the plague, Prokop the Great assumed command of the Hussite forces. His leadership was crucial in continuing the Hussite resistance during the ongoing conflicts in Bohemia.

events.name: Crown Prince Designation in Ming Dynasty
events.enhanced_description: Emperor Renzong of the Ming dynasty designated his son, Zhu Zhanji, as Crown Prince. This decision set the stage for Zhu Zhanji's eventual ascension to the throne as Emperor Xuanzong.

events.name: Installation of the Bourges Astronomical Clock
events.enhanced_description: The Bourges astronomical clock, designed by Jean Fusoris, was installed in Bourges Cathedral as a gift from King Charles VII to the town. This clock was a significant advancement in astronomical technology and reflected the growing interest in science during the Renaissance.

events.name: Radu II Chelul Becomes Prince of Wallachia
events.enhanced_description: Radu II Chelul ascended to the throne of Wallachia for the third time, taking over from Dan II following an Ottoman invasion. His reign was marked by the challenges of maintaining power amid external threats.

events.name: Offer of Hvar to the Republic of Venice
events.enhanced_description: Aliota Capenna, the lord of Hvar, offered his realm to the Republic of Venice, a significant political maneuver during the period of Venetian expansion in the Adriatic. This offer reflected the complex political landscape of Dalmatia.

events.name: Battle of St. James
events.enhanced_description: In the Battle of St. James near Avranches, an English army led by John, Duke of Bedford, defeated the French forces under Arthur de Richemont. This victory reinforced English control in Normandy during the Hundred Years' War.

events.name: Fleeing of Kale Kye-Taung Nyo
events.enhanced_description: Kale Kye-Taung Nyo, ruler of the Kingdom of Ava, fled his capital, leading to the succession of Mohnyin Thado. This transition marked a significant shift in the power dynamics of the region.

events.name: Battle of Usti nad Labem

locations.name: Ústí nad Labem, Ústí nad Labem Region, Czech Republic

events.enhanced_description: In the Battle of Usti nad Labem, the Hussites achieved a decisive victory over the crusading armies during the Fourth Anti-Hussite Crusade. This battle was a pivotal moment in the Hussite Wars, showcasing the resilience of the Hussite forces.

events.name: Battle of Khirokitia
events.enhanced_description: In the Battle of Khirokitia, King Janus of Cyprus was defeated and captured by the Mamluks. He was subsequently taken to Egypt, where he was held for ten months before being ransomed, highlighting the turbulent political landscape of the region.

events.name: Construction of Castello Orsini-Odescalchi
events.enhanced_description: The Castello Orsini-Odescalchi was constructed in Bracciano by the Orsini family, serving as a significant architectural and cultural landmark in Italy. This castle reflects the feudal power and influence of the Orsini family during the Renaissance.

events.name: Lincoln College founded
events.enhanced_description: Lincoln College, a constituent college of the University of Oxford, was founded by the Bishop of Lincoln in 1427. It has since become one of the prominent colleges within the university, known for its rich history and academic excellence.

events.name: Gabriel V elected Patriarch
events.enhanced_description: Gabriel V was elected as the Patriarch of the Coptic Church for the second time in 1427. His leadership was significant in the context of the Coptic Christian community in Egypt during a period of political and religious challenges.

events.name: Minrekyansa becomes King of Ava
events.enhanced_description: Minrekyansa ascended to the throne as the King of Ava in 1427, marking a significant moment in the history of the Burmese monarchy. His reign contributed to the consolidation of power in the region during a time of political fragmentation.

events.name: Conflict of Druimnacour
events.enhanced_description: The Conflict of Druimnacour took place in Sutherland, Scotland, in 1427. This skirmish was part of the ongoing power struggles among Scottish clans during a tumultuous period in Scottish history.

events.name: First witch hunts begin
events.enhanced_description: The first witch hunts began in Switzerland in 1427, marking the start of a dark chapter in European history characterized by superstition and persecution. These hunts would escalate in intensity over the following decades, leading to widespread fear and injustice.

events.name: Celestine Order established
events.enhanced_description: The Celestine Order was established in France in 1427, contributing to the monastic landscape of the time. This order emphasized a contemplative lifestyle and played a role in the spiritual revival of the period.

events.name: Celebration of Sant Jordi begins
events.enhanced_description: The Celebration of Sant Jordi (Saint George) began in Catalonia in 1427, evolving into a significant cultural event that celebrates love and literature. This tradition continues to be a cherished part of Catalan identity.

events.name: Bremen expelled from Hanseatic League
events.enhanced_description: In 1427, Bremen was expelled from the Hanseatic League, a powerful economic alliance of merchant guilds and towns in Northern Europe. This expulsion marked a significant shift in the city's political and economic landscape.

events.name: Diogo de Silves discovers Azores
events.enhanced_description: In 1427, Portuguese navigator Diogo de Silves discovered seven islands of the Azores archipelago, which would later become an important strategic location for maritime navigation and trade in the Atlantic.

events.name: Battle of the Echinades
events.enhanced_description: The Battle of the Echinades occurred in 1427, where a Byzantine fleet successfully defeated the forces of Carlo I Tocco. This victory was part of the ongoing conflicts in the region during the decline of Byzantine power.

events.name: Itzcoatl becomes Tlatoani of Tenochtitlan
events.enhanced_description: In 1427, Itzcoatl became the 4th Tlatoani of Tenochtitlan following the assassination of his nephew Chimalpopoca. His reign marked the beginning of the expansion of the Aztec Empire and the consolidation of power in the Valley of Mexico.

events.name: Bhaktapur Royal Palace built
events.enhanced_description: The Bhaktapur Royal Palace was built by King Yaksa Malla in 1427, showcasing the architectural grandeur of the Malla dynasty. This palace remains a significant historical site, reflecting the rich cultural heritage of Nepal.

events.name: Catalonia earthquake
